#### 2.3.1 Round 1 report (verbatim)

`````markdown
# Johnny Meier's Whole Lineage: Standouts, Cousins and Regional Ties

*Research completed 7 Oct 2026. It builds on John's two earlier reports ("Old Records Reshape Johnny Meier's Family Tree" and "Family ties to Hauppauge") and the Bull Smith lineage PDF, which override the Ancestry tree where they conflict. The Ancestry tree itself came from the 49 screenshots in the project's Google Drive folder. Detailed notes with a source link on every claim are in [research/notes/](/mnt/project-files/research/notes/). Labels: **confirmed** (a record or well-sourced compilation states it), **probable** (strong fit, one document short), **speculative** (a lead).*

## The short version

- **Northeastern Pennsylvania is the family's center of gravity, on both sides.** Every branch that reached America in the last 230 years settled in the anthracite valleys:
  - **The Meiers** were in Hazleton, then Wilkes-Barre.
  - **The Pringle, Lamoreaux, Croup, Scott and Heffernan lines** were in Plymouth, Kingston and Larksville.
  - **The mother's Italian lines** (Petriello, Cognetti, Ferlaino) were in Scranton and Dunmore.
- **Long Island is the deep root.** It is entirely colonial, from 1640 to about 1760, through Smithtown, Southampton, Southold, Setauket and Moriches. No 19th- or 20th-century Long Island tie turned up for any line.
- **Virginia has no ancestor, only cousins.** No direct ancestor in any line lived in Virginia. The one genuine Virginia blood tie is new: **First Lady Julia Gardiner Tyler**, wife of President John Tyler, and her Virginia-born Tyler children are cousins through Bull Smith.
- **The closest notable relatives are on the mother's side.** Johnny's grandmother Mary Cognetti Petriello had two brothers of note:
  - **Anthony R. Cognetti** was president of Scranton City Council.
  - **Joseph F. Cognetti** was a WWII Army Air Corps veteran inducted into the Candy Hall of Fame.
- **The tree needs several new fixes on top of the 30 already flagged.** The biggest:
  - Jerusha Topping's parents are wrong, so the whole Sayre branch comes off.
  - The Youngs ancestry is unproven.
  - "Captain" Johann C. Doll was not a captain.
  - The Italian tree has a pair of duplicated parents.

---

## 1. Individuals who stand out

### Direct ancestors
| Person | Why notable | Region | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux (6th-great-grandfather) | Revolutionary patriot (SAR P-232580), Orange Co. NY militia; Plymouth PA pioneer | NE PA / NY | Confirmed (earlier report). **Still Johnny's only proven patriot route.** |
| Richard "Bull" Smith (10th-great-grandfather) | Founder and patentee of Smithtown | Long Island | Confirmed (earlier report) |
| William Wells (10th-great-grandfather) | Southold founder, High Sheriff of Yorkshire, Gov. Nicolls's council | Long Island | Confirmed; this is the Society of Colonial Wars route, once Capt. John Tuttle's parents are proven |
| Capt. Thomas Topping (now **11th**-great-grandfather, one generation further back than reported) | Captain, magistrate, Connecticut deputy | Long Island | Probable (see correction 3a) |
| Johann Andreas Grub (6th-great-grandfather) | Palatine immigrant (Jettenbach, ship *Phoenix* 1754); landowner beside the Delaware at Easton, near today's Lafayette College | Easton PA | Confirmed |
| Frederick Croup (5th-great-grandfather) | Owned "Stewart's Flats" in Plymouth, where Asa Upson was killed in a 1780 Indian raid; his farm was the landing for the "Dutch Fishery" shad haul | NE PA | Probable |

### Close relatives (great-uncles and their generation)

|---|---|---|---|
| **Anthony R. Cognetti** (d. 2008) | Great-uncle (brother of grandmother Mary Cognetti) | WWII Army veteran; **president of Scranton City Council**; president of the Scranton Red Sox collegiate baseball club | Confirmed |
| **Joseph F. Cognetti** (1919–2009) | Great-uncle | WWII Army Air Corps 1942–46; chairman of D.C. Sales Co.; **Candy Hall of Fame 1975**, AWMA Hall of Fame 1993; started the family's 50-year Cognetti Thanksgiving (151 relatives in 2016) | Confirmed |
| **Maj. Leo G. Heffernan** | 2nd-great-grand-uncle | West Point; Army pilot #489; Pershing's "chief air scout" in the 1916 Mexican Expedition; commanded Wilbur Wright Field | Confirmed (earlier report) |

| Thomas Pringle (1791–1861) | 4th-great-grand-uncle | Coal operator; likely namesake of Pringle Borough | Probable (earlier report) |
| Philip Grub/Croop (1753–1812) | 5th-great-grand-uncle | Revolutionary militia private, Northampton Co. 1777–80. He is collateral, so his service **cannot** be used for SAR/DAR | Confirmed |

### Distant cousins (new in this round)
| Cousin | Relationship | Through | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **First Lady Julia Gardiner Tyler** (1820–1889) | **5th cousin 6x removed** | Bull Smith → Richard 2d → Nathaniel Smith → Mary Smith (m. Col. Abraham Gardiner) | Confirmed in two independent published genealogies |
| Sen. David Gardiner (killed in the 1844 USS *Princeton* explosion) | 4C7R | same | Confirmed |
| **Rep. David Gardiner Tyler** (1846–1927): Confederate soldier, U.S. Representative from **Virginia** | 6C5R | same | Confirmed |
| **Lyon Gardiner Tyler** (1853–1935): president of the College of **William & Mary** | 6C5R | same | Confirmed |
| Harrison Ruffin Tyler (1928–2025): restored Sherwood Forest Plantation, Virginia | 7C4R | same | Confirmed |

| Judge Isaac Thompson of Sagtikos Manor | 2C9R | Thompson | Confirmed |

The earlier reports' cousins still stand: Gen. Nathaniel Woodhull, Col. Jesse Woodhull, William Floyd, the Culper Ring men, Anna Symmes Harrison, President Benjamin Harrison, Rear Adm. Theodorus Bailey, and the Hauppauge Judge and Senator Joshua Smith. **One adjustment:** the "via Topping" figures each gain one "removed" (e.g. Gen. Woodhull's 3C8R via Topping becomes 3C9R). Routes via Bull Smith are unchanged.

**"Tippecanoe and Tyler Too":** both First Ladies of that 1840 ticket, Anna Harrison and Julia Tyler, are Johnny's blood cousins. Neither president is.

### Same surname, same hometown, kinship unproven
- **Judge Francesco Ferlaino** (1914–1975) was murdered by the 'Ndrangheta. **Corrado Ferlaino** was SSC Napoli's owner in the Maradona era. Both families came from Conflenti, next door to the Ferlaino hometown of San Mango d'Aquino.
- **Paige Cognetti, Mayor of Scranton**, married into *a* Scranton Cognetti family. Whether it is Johnny's was not researched, because the people involved are living.
- **Not related:** PFC Frank A. Petriello (killed in Germany in 1945) was from Bayonne, NJ.
- **Not kin:** the Sayres (Stephen Sayre, Francis B. Sayre) and the Oyster Bay Youngses (see corrections 3a and 3b).

---

## 2. Regional ties

### Northeastern Pennsylvania (strong, every American line)
| Line | Place | Period | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meier: Freiderich & Maria (Birkenmayer) | **Hazleton**, where they died 19 Feb 1913 and 30 Dec 1911 | to 1913 | Probable (PA death index, files 14339 and 113353) |
| Meier: William F. & Florence Pringle | Wilkes-Barre; William died there 4 Jul 1963 | 1920s–1963 | Probable (PA death index, file 071200) |
| Pringle, Lamoreaux, Croup, Scott | Plymouth, Kingston, Hunlock Creek, Nanticoke | 1790–1943 | Confirmed |
| Heffernan, Connole | Larksville, Plymouth, Wilkes-Barre | 1860s–1947 | Confirmed |
| Petriello, Di Biase | **Dunmore (Bunker Hill section) / Scranton.** Hometown colony from Guardia Lombardi, which founded St. Rocco's Church in 1905 | c.1890– | Confirmed for John Petriello (1869–1939) |
| Cognetti; Ferlaino, Fiorillo | **Scranton (Providence section).** Home of the San Mango d'Aquino Mutual Benefit Society | c.1910– | Confirmed for Frank & Helen Cognetti's family |
| McGuire: Francis McGuire & Elizabeth McAvoy | Probably the Wyoming Valley; not yet placed | — | Speculative |

### Long Island (colonial only)
- **Smithtown and Nissequogue:** Bull Smith and Job Smith's home lots. James Smith's 1736 tract bordered the Hauppauge estate.
- **Moriches:** James Smith & Jerusha Topping settled here.
- **Southampton, Sagaponack and Bridgehampton:** the Toppings. Bull Smith's first home lot was on Southampton's main street.
- **Southold, Cutchogue and Mattituck:** William Wells and the Tuthills.
- **Setauket:** John Thompson's home lot faced the village green.
- **Cousin sites:** Gardiner's Island and East Hampton (Julia Tyler's birthplace); Sagtikos Manor (the Thompsons); Hauppauge (the Smith judges).
- **No later tie found:** nothing places the Meiers, McGuires or Petriellos on Long Island in the 1900s. If the family moved there, Kathryn (McGuire) Meier's 1970 death in the New York State Death Index is the first place to check.

### Virginia (cousins only)
- **Genuine blood tie:** the Tylers of Sherwood Forest, Charles City County, through Julia Gardiner Tyler.
- **Not blood ties:**
  - The Virginia Harrisons of Berkeley Plantation. Benjamin Harrison is kin only through his Long Island grandmother Anna Symmes.
  - Stephen Sayre, who died in Brandon, Virginia; the Sayre line is not Johnny's.
  - Roger Ludlow and Col. Richard Townley, both in-laws only.
  - A Bretten Doll family that moved to Augusta County, Virginia. It is a different family that online trees often merge with Johnny's Dolls.
- **No direct ancestor, and no Revolutionary service in Virginia, was found in any line.**

---

## 3. Corrections to add to the tree

These come on top of the 30 already listed in the earlier report.

**Colonial lines**
- **3a. Jerusha Topping's parents.** They were **Elnathan Topping (1664–1751) & Mary**, not Josiah Topping & Hannah Sayre. Howell (1887) lists a Jerusha in Elnathan's will, and the Sayre genealogy gives Josiah & Hannah only two sons. Remove Josiah Topping, Hannah Sayre, John Topping (1636–1686) and the Sayres. This also fixes the date problem the Hauppauge report raised. *Probable.*
- **3b. Mary "Youngs," wife of William Wells.** Both standard genealogies (Hayes 1878, Youngs 1907) reject her as Rev. John Youngs's daughter; that daughter married Edward Petty. Mark Rev. John Youngs, Vicar Christopher Youngs and the "Horne" ancestors as **unproven**.
- **3c. William Wells's parents.** "Rev. William Wells to the Queen of Denmark" garbles a Norwich prebendary who was chaplain to Queen Anne of Denmark. He is a possible father, by family tradition only. The "Anne Elizabeth Hunt Kimball" mother is unsupported.
- **3d. Bull Smith's parents.** "Sir Samuel Smith & Rebecca Buswell" are unsupported, so remove them. His wife Sarah Hammond was the daughter of **William Hammond of Watertown, MA**, a newly identified 11th-great-grandfather.
- **3e. Hannah Brewster** (wife of John Thompson) was a daughter of Francis Brewster of New Haven. She was **not** of the Mayflower Brewster family.
- **3f. Tree versus PDF.** The tree shows "Justice Adam Smith" as James Smith's father; the PDF is right that it was **Job Smith**.

**Pennsylvania lines**
- **3g. "Johann C. Doll, Captain."** He is **Johann Casper Doll** of Ulmet (bapt. 1722, d. 1793, Plainfield Twp.) and was not a captain. The captaincy, the 1934 monument and the flag photo belong to his nephew Capt. Casper Dull (1748–1829). Whether Anna Maria Doll was Casper's daughter is unproven.
- **3h. Add missing ancestors.**
  - Maria Elisabetha Christmann (1729–1815), wife of Andrew Grub.
  - Susan Croup Shupp, Elizabeth's sister, who independently confirms Frederick & Mary (Young) Croup.
- **3i. Scott dates.**
  - Stephen Scott was born c.1797 or earlier (not 1808) and died 1855.
  - Julia Ann was born c.1799, not 1809.
  - Both were born in Connecticut.
  - The surname "Watson" is unsourced.

**Meier and McGuire**
- **3j. Middle initials and dates.**
  - William is **William F.** Meier.
  - James is **James C.** Meier, born 13 Jul 1928 (probable).
  - Kathryn F. McGuire was born 22 Aug 1930 to **Francis McGuire & Elizabeth McAvoy** (probable). Add them.
- **3k. Henry J. Meier's 1940 death** is not in the Pennsylvania index under any spelling. Either he died out of state or the year is wrong.

**Italian lines**
- **3l. Claudia Di Vivo** has been given her husband Claudio Gialanella's parents. Remove them.
- **3m. Cognetti siblings.**
  - The two "Ralph Cognetti 1913" entries are one man: Ralph A. Cognetti (7 Aug 1913 – 2009).
  - "Levyso" is **Leo S. Cognetti** (c.1929–2019).
  - Joseph was born in 1919, not 1918.
- **3n. Mollie Petriello** (b. 1911) is James Petriello's wife, not Mary Cognetti. Her maiden name is unknown.
- **3o. Helen Cognetti's maiden name conflicts.** The tree says **Ferlaino**; Anthony Cognetti's 2008 obituary says "Helen **Farina** Cognetti." The whole Fiorillo/Morrello/Guercio pedigree hangs on this.
- **3p. Identical dates and dubious attachments.**
  - Several couples share identical dates (Dimarino/Magnotta 1760–1808, D'Ambrosio/Giordano d. 1819), which look copied.
  - The "Lucera, Foggia" record on Domenico Di Biase is probably attached to the wrong man. The family was from Guardia Lombardi in Avellino.

---

## 4. The lines researched for the first time

**The Petriello line came from Guardia Lombardi, Avellino.**
- **Confirmed:** Giovanni "John" Petriello was born there on 25 Oct 1869, son of Pietro Petriello & Grazia di Marino, and married Maria Antonia DiBiasi. He came to the US about 1889–95 and died in Scranton in 1939. James Petriello (1911–1998) is probably their son "James Petrillo."
- **Probable:** the Di Biase, Siconolfi, Gialanella, Magnotta and Di Marino ancestors were from the same town. Gialanella, Magnotta and Siconolfi all have Guardia as their top place of origin, and Guardia even has a hamlet called Case Siconolfi.

**The Cognetta line probably came from Dasà, now in Vibo Valentia province, Calabria.**
- **Probable:** a Nicola Cognetta married to a Cannatello born in Dasà in 1818 matches the tree's Nicola Cognetta & Mariantonia Cannatello.
- **Confirmed:** Frank Cognetti was in Scranton by 1913.

**The Ferlaino and Fiorillo line probably came from San Mango d'Aquino, Catanzaro.**
- **Probable:** five of the branch's surnames (Ferlaino, Fiorillo, Colosimo, Fata, Marsico) are typical of the town.
- **Confirmed:** a Ferlaino household at 1306 Diamond Ave, Scranton, took in boarders from San Mango.
- **Not identified:** the black coat of arms with a silver lion on the Fiorillo profiles matches none of the 35 nearby comuni checked. It may have been copied from another family's tree.

**Meier, Higgins and McGuire:** see 2 and 3j–3k. No notable relative was proven in these lines. Anna Higgins's origin is still unknown.

**Croup/Grub, Young and Doll:**
- **Confirmed:** these were Palatine Germans from Jettenbach and Ulmet, a few kilometres apart in the Kusel district. They came through Philadelphia and Easton, and Frederick Croup moved to the Hunlock's Creek/Nanticoke river flats about 1800.
- **Probable:** the Croop sawmills, and later the Croop's Glen amusement park, descend from Frederick's nephews' line, not his own.

---

## 5. Records that would settle the most

1. **PA death certificates** with known file numbers: Frederick Meier 1913 #14339 and Mary A. Meier 1911 #113353 (both Hazleton), and William F. Meier 1963 #071200. They should give Frederick's German birthplace, his parents, and William's parents, which tests the Henry J. Meier–Anna Higgins link.
2. **The Lackawanna County marriage license** of Frank Cognetti & Helen (c.1912–13). It settles Ferlaino vs. Farina.
3. **Kathryn Meier's 1970 death record:** the New York index if she died there, otherwise a PA certificate request. Her SS-5 application should name her birthplace and parents.
4. **Antenati civil records** for Guardia Lombardi (John Petriello's 1869 birth act), San Mango d'Aquino (the Ferlaino × Fiorillo marriage and Helen's birth) and Dasà (Giovanni Cognetta's 1855 birth).
5. **The colonial gaps:**
   - The 1967 F. K. Smith genealogy entry for James Smith, and Elnathan Topping's 1751 will, to settle Temperance Smith's parents and the Topping generation.
   - Akerly and Tuttle compilations, to settle Capt. John Tuttle's father.
6. **The SAR/DAR databases**, searched by hand in a browser (automated searches were blocked), for Casper Doll, John Young and Andrew Grub. Patriotic service such as an oath of allegiance or supplies would also count.

*Access limits this round: Ancestry, Find a Grave, FamilySearch record search, Antenati, Geni and Legacy all blocked automated access. Several findings therefore rest on public indexes and search-engine extracts, and are labelled probable rather than confirmed. Living people were not researched beyond the names already in the tree.*
`````

`````markdown
# Johnny Meier Lineage: Round 2 Deep Dive (October 2026)

This report builds on the first report, `Johnny_Meier_Lineage_Report_2026-10.md`, and doesn't repeat it. Each finding is labelled:

- **Confirmed**: a record I read says so directly, or two independent records agree.

## 1. The short version

- **The flyer in the family.** Maj. Leo G. Heffernan, a brother of great-great-grandmother Catherine Heffernan Pringle, set a **250-mph speed record on 24 Mar 1923**, which *Time* covered. He later ran the Army Air Corps Technical School and commanded France Field in Panama. His obituary says **Jimmy Doolittle and Claire Chennault served under him**.
- **A mayor, a senator and a Titanic victim are among your cousins.** Through Bull Smith and the Long Island lines, you are cousin to:

- **The Irish line now reaches County Tipperary.** The Heffernans came from the parish of **Killenaule and Gortnahoe** in Co. Tipperary. They were coal miners there before they mined anthracite in Pennsylvania. Two great-uncles were **transported to Australia** after a constable was killed in 1834.
- **Your grandmother Mollie is identified.** "Mollie" Petriello was **Carmela Gianetta** (1910–2000) of Dunmore. Her parents came from **Bisaccia**, a second Irpinian hometown alongside Guardia Lombardi.

- **The Long Island gap is now probably closed.** Temperance Smith's parents (James Smith and Jerusha Topping) and John Tuthill's father are now probable, from a 1968 Tuttle genealogy.

## 4. Stories and interesting facts

### Colonial Long Island and the Hudson Valley

- **Bull Smith's reluctant wedding.** Richard "Bull" Smith tried to back out of marrying Sarah Hammond in 1640. The marriage went ahead anyway and founded the whole Smithtown line.
- **"Old Crib."** Sarah Hammond Smith's blunderbuss, "Old Crib", was passed down in the family as an heirloom.
- **A colt, on conditions.** William Hammond's will left his grandson Adam a colt "if he behave obediently."
- **The Phantom Ship.** Francis Brewster was lost aboard New Haven's "Great Shippe" in 1646. A ghostly image of that ship was later said to appear over the harbor.
- **"Wast paper."** Francis Brewster's widow Lucy was tried in 1646 for calling the minister's sermon "wast paper."
- **Topping's Purchase.** Land on eastern Long Island was bought from the Native owners with wampum.
- **Saved from the navy.** In 1706 Governor Cornbury ordered André Lamoureux released after he had been impressed into naval service.
- **A pointed will.** Thomas Lamoreaux's 1829 will disinherited his son James and left a share to his disabled grandson Jewel. It also left his wife Keturah his best horse.
- **A family regiment.** In 1776 two of Keturah's Smith uncles were militia captains, and her future husband's family served as officers under them.

### Ireland to Pennsylvania (the Heffernans)

- **Miners twice over.** The Heffernans dug coal in the Slieveardagh hills of Tipperary, one of Ireland's few coalfields, before they dug anthracite in Luzerne County.
- **Transported to Australia.** Great-uncles James and Patrick Heffernan were sent to New South Wales after Constable Feeney was killed at Ballynonty in 1834.
- **A shooting at Leadville.** Anna Heffernan Dillon's husband was shot in the Colorado silver boomtown of Leadville in 1880.
- **The Sunday paper.** Thomas F. Heffernan's *Sunday Independent* is digitized for 1913–58 on POWER Library. It is a good place to look for family notices.

### Italy (Irpinia and Calabria)

- **Guardia Lombardi** was founded by the Lombards around 571–591 as a lookout fort. A plague in 1656 killed 1,110 of its 1,475 people. The 1980 Irpinia earthquake destroyed more than half its buildings.
- **St. Rocco's in Dunmore.** About 40 families from Guardia bought a former Presbyterian church there and said the first Mass in October 1905. John Petriello's grocery, already open by 1897, would have served that early colony.
- **Bisaccia**, Mollie's family's town, sent about 916 people to America between 1830 and 1912, with the peak in 1906, the year Frank Giannetta came. Mario Procaccino, the 1969 Democratic nominee for mayor of New York City, was born there; no kinship is known.
- **San Mango d'Aquino** was founded in the early 1600s by a branch of the d'Aquino family, the family of St. Thomas Aquinas, and its church is dedicated to him. The Ferlaino house at 1306 Diamond Ave took in newly arrived San Mango men as boarders.

### Black Forest

- **The Jägerhof.** In 1751 Josef Heitzler, gamekeeper to the Counts of Kageneck, bought the farm later called the Jägerhof at auction. Its sawmill still operates. Josef Heitzler "vom Jägerhof" was mayor of Unteribental from 1919 to 1924.
- **The youngest son inherits.** Black Forest farms passed whole to one son, usually the youngest. The other children became weavers, sawyers, gamekeepers or emigrants.
- **A one-way ticket.** In 1861 Kirchzarten paid half the fare to send Xaver Ruh, a repeat thief, to America rather than see him steal a fourth time.
- **Kirchzarten was part of Austria.** The city of Freiburg owned Kirchzarten from 1492 to 1805, within Habsburg "Further Austria", before it passed to Baden.

### Pennsylvania in the 1900s

- **The Lattimer Massacre** of 1897 took place just outside Hazleton while Freiderich and Maria Meier lived there.
- **The Agnes flood** of 1972 washed graves out of the Forty Fort cemetery.
- **Levittown, PA** was built between 1952 and 1958. In 1957 it drew national headlines when the Myers family, its first Black residents, faced mob harassment.

---

## 5. Regional ties, updated

- **Long Island.** The ties are still colonial only, but stronger: Smithtown, the Tuthills, Topping's Purchase and the Lawrence cousins. Two speculative Henry Meier deaths, at Huntington (1931) and Hempstead (1937), are the only possible modern link.
- **Northeastern PA.** Every American line converges here:
  - the Meiers in Hazleton and then Wilkes-Barre;
  - the Pringles and Heffernans in Plymouth and Wilkes-Barre;
  - the Petriellos, Gianettas, Cognettis and Ferlainos in Scranton and Dunmore.

  James C. Meier's death in Levittown, Bucks County, is the first record of the family outside the coal region.
- **Virginia.** Nothing new. First Lady Julia Gardiner Tyler is still the only cousin tie.

---

## 6. Records that would settle the open questions

1. **Pennsylvania death certificates:**
   - Frederick Meier, 1913 #14339
   - Mary A. Meier, 1911 #113353
   - William F. Meier, 1963 #071200

   William's certificate would prove or disprove Henry J. Meier and Anna Higgins as his parents.
2. **Kathryn Meier's 1970 PA death certificate.** Also her Social Security application (SS-5) through a FOIA request.
3. **James C. Meier's obituary**, in the *Bucks County Courier Times* for Aug 2008.
4. **Munzingen Catholic baptisms** (Staatsarchiv Freiburg, collection L 10) for 1807, 1837 and 15 Mar 1842. These would settle Servatius and the Heitzler question.
5. **Helen Cognetti's PA death certificate** would confirm Ferlaino. **Frank Cognetti's 1942 WWII draft card** would give his birth town.
6. **Guardia civil records** for Grazia Di Marino's birth, to settle whether her mother was di Leo or d'Ambrosio.
7. **NY death certificates #44888 and #34005**, the two Long Island Henry Meier deaths.
`````

#### 2.3.3 Round 3 report (verbatim)

`````markdown
# Johnny Meier Lineage, Round 3: Confirmations and Origins (October 2026)

This round had three goals:

1. Turn "probable" links into "confirmed" ones.
2. Trace the Meier surname line as far back as the records go.
3. Pin every family line to a specific town and specific people in Germany, Italy, England, France and Ireland.

It builds on the Round 1 and Round 2 reports and does not repeat them.

**How confident each finding is:**

- **Confirmed** means I read the original record image, or two independent records agree.
- **Probable** means strong evidence that still lacks one deciding document.
- **Speculative** means a lead only.

**Where the details are:** full sources and record links are in `research/notes/round3/`. There is one file each for the Meier line, the other German lines, the Italian lines, the English and French lines, and the Irish and Pennsylvania lines. Living people were not researched.

---

## 1. The short version

- **The Meier line is now proven, generation by generation, from your grandfather back to a carpenter born in the 1700s.**
  - It runs James C. → William F. → Henry J. → Friedrich → Heinrich → Michael Mayer.
  - The family came from **Munzingen**, a wine village just west of Freiburg im Breisgau in Baden. It was not Kirchzarten.
  - Every US link comes from census pages and marriage applications. Every German link comes from the original Munzingen civil registers.
- **The Birkenmayers were from Munzingen too.** Maria Anna Birkenmayer, Friedrich's wife, was born there in 1837. Her parents and grandparents are confirmed there as well, back to a Johann Ev. Birkenmayer born in 1771.
- **Your Italian lines now reach the early 1800s in four towns.** The Guardia Lombardi line reaches a couple married before about 1796, Pietro di Marino and Felicita Magnotta. The other three towns are Bisaccia, Dasà and San Mango d'Aquino.
- **Your Italian great-great-grandmother was a foundling.** Angelica Ferrantino, Mollie's mother, was left as a baby at **Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi** around 1873. Her parents are unknown.
- **Your English roots are in specific parishes.**
  - Tuthill: Tharston and Saxlingham, Norfolk.
  - Hammond and Paine: Lavenham and Long Melford, Suffolk.
  - Topping: Totternhoe, Bedfordshire.
  - Horton: Mowsley, Leicestershire.
- **Your French roots are Huguenot, from Saintonge on the Atlantic coast.**
  - The Lamoureux were from Meschers-sur-Gironde.
  - The Mersereau, Masse and Dubois families were from Moëze, near Rochefort.
- **Your Irish roots are in Co. Tipperary.** The Heffernan and Boney families lived at Lickfinn and Mardyke in the Slieveardagh coalfield. This is now confirmed.
- **One line has to come out.** The **Brewster** ancestry, Francis and Lucy Brewster of New Haven, is probably not yours. The cousins found "via Brewster" in Round 2 go with it. One journal article still needs to be read directly before this is final.

---

## 2. The Meier line, generation by generation

| Gen | Person | What the records show | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **James C. Meier** (b. 13 Jul 1928) | In the household of William F. and Florence Meier in the 1930 and 1950 Wilkes-Barre censuses; listed as "James C", 21, in 1950. Died 13 Aug 2008, Levittown, PA. | Parents **Confirmed**. Death Probable. |
| 2 | **William F. Meier** (c.1904–1963) | Born in **Tamaqua**, Schuylkill Co. Married Florence Louise Pringle at Wilkes-Barre on 20 Apr 1926; marriage application No. 10768 names his parents as Henry (moulder) and Anna Higgins. He worked in coal-company offices all his life: clerk in 1926 and 1930, supervisor in 1950. | **Confirmed** |
| 3 | **Henry J. Meier** (15 Nov 1866 – 1940) | Born in Baden, Germany. Came to America as a toddler in **1868**. Married **Annie A. Higgins** at Hazleton on 1 Mar 1892 (docket #11054). She was born 2 Oct 1867 in New Philadelphia, Schuylkill Co. He worked as an iron **moulder** for nearly 50 years and was still at an iron works at 72 in the 1940 census, living at 16 Barney St. | **Confirmed**. His death certificate is still not found. |
| 4 | **Friedrich Mayer / Frederick Meier** (2 Mar 1835 – 19 Feb 1913) | **Born at Munzingen.** Married Maria Anna Birkenmaier there on 20 Oct 1862. A **stone mason** in Hazleton, PA, in the 1870 and 1880 censuses. Both censuses list Henry as his son, born in Baden. In 1880 the household included "Gabriel Bergenmyer", his brother-in-law. He and Maria had 11 children; she died 30 Dec 1911 and he died 19 Feb 1913, both in Hazleton. | **Confirmed** (original German registers and US censuses) |
| 5 | **Heinrich ("Henericus") Mayer** (c.1796 – after 1862) | A **mason**, later a master mason. Married **Juliana Senn** at Munzingen on 16 Oct 1820, when he was 24 and she was 22. They lived in house No. 68. Juliana was an orphan, the illegitimate daughter of another Juliana Senn. | **Confirmed** |
| 6 | **Michael Mayer** | **Citizen and carpenter of Munzingen.** His wife and dates are not yet found. | **Confirmed** (named as Heinrich's father in the 1820 marriage) |

**Building trades for four generations.** Michael was a carpenter, Heinrich a mason, Friedrich a stone mason and Henry an iron moulder.

**Other family members:**

- **Henry's siblings:** Frederick (born 1862 in Germany), Frances, Mary, Clarissa, Elizabeth, Theresa, Anna, Agatha, Sophia and John Joseph.
- **William's siblings:** Fred Aloysius, Henry Jr., Mary C., Madeline and Joseph John.
- **Friedrich's sister:** Maria Anna Creszentia, born 3 Jul 1821.

**When the family emigrated:** in 1868, by Henry's own account. Friedrich, Maria and their four small children came over together. The ship has not been found. The Bremen emigrant database has no match, so they may have sailed from Le Havre or Antwerp.

**Records that would take the line further back:**

- Heinrich's baptism around 1796, which is in the Munzingen Catholic parish book, before the civil registers begin.
- Michael Mayer's death entry, in the Munzingen death registers for 1810–39.
- The emigration files at the Staatsarchiv Freiburg.

**Corrections:**

- **Maria Birkenmayer's mother was Agatha Heizler, not "Maria Anna Heitzler".** Agatha was born 26 Jun 1813 to Joseph Heizler, a gamekeeper for the Counts of Kageneck, and M. Anna Federer.
- **Federer is a Munzingen family.** It is not the Black Forest Fürderer family.
- **Servatius Birkenmayer** was born at Munzingen on 4 May 1807. He was a master glazier, and he died there on 19 Apr 1853.
- **The tree's "Johann E. Birkenmaier 1771–1844 and Magdalena Erb" is correct after all.** Round 2 had called it unsupported.
- **Casper Doll arrived on the ship *Samuel* on 27 Aug 1739**, aged 18, not in 1737.

## 5. Stories from this round

- **A pilot of the Gironde.** André Lamoureux guided ships through the dangerous mouth of the Gironde. He fled France with his family and lost a son at Bristol in 1690. He was naturalized by Act of Parliament in 1694. In 1706 the governor of New York ordered him released after he had been forced into the Royal Navy.
- **A Huguenot wedding season.** In the summer of 1693, New York's French Church married three Mersereau siblings in three weeks. Your ancestor Pierre Masse signed as witness every time, and the widowed mother Elisabet Dubois made her mark.
- **The three friars (family legend).** Jean Mersereau supposedly greeted three disguised friars with "Good evening, gentlemen", saying he knew "but one Father, who is in Heaven". When they drew hidden swords, he fought them off. This is a genuine family tradition but not proven history.
- **The water bailiff who helped found Connecticut.** In 1636 Thomas Topping reported to the Wraysbury manor court that "all was well with the water courses". Wraysbury parish contains Magna Carta Island. In 1662 he was named in King Charles II's charter for Connecticut.
- **Lavenham clothiers.** William Hammond was born in one of England's richest wool towns, and his great-grandfather was a fuller. William's wife sailed to New England in 1634 with three children, including your ancestor Sarah.
- **The reluctant bridegroom.** In 1640 Bull Smith petitioned to be released from his promise to marry Sarah Hammond. He lost, and their marriage founded the Smithtown line. In 1656 he may have sailed back from England on the same ship as the first Quaker missionaries to New England.
- **Stonemasons from a wine village.** Munzingen sits on the Tuniberg vineyards under the Counts of Kageneck, whose castle (Schloss) dates from 1672. Friedrich Mayer's next-door neighbour in Hazleton in 1870 was another Baden stone mason, a sign of a small Baden building-trades network.
- **A brother-in-law with "fever & ague".** Gabriel Birkenmayer was sick with a malaria-type fever on census day in 1880, while living with his sister's family. He and his brother Joseph later went to Sandusky, Ohio.
- **From slate picker to clerk.** In 1880 Addison Pringle's 13-year-old brother Orange picked slate in a coal breaker. Two generations later, both of your paternal grandparents' parents were clerks and bookkeepers. In 1910 the Pringle and McGuire families lived in the same small town, Larksville, 18 years before their children married.
- **A foundling's name.** "Ferrantino" was probably assigned to Angelica at the foundling wheel of Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi.
- **Shepherds and candle-makers.** The Giannettas and Fedes of Bisaccia were shepherds. In 1855 Nicola Cognetta of Dasà was styled "Mastro", a master craftsman: he was a candle-maker, making votive and church candles.
- **A Tipperary miner's son.** The Heffernans dug coal in the Slieveardagh hills of Tipperary before they dug anthracite in Luzerne County.

## 6. The records that would settle what is still open

1. **Henry J. Meier's 1940 death certificate**, or his burial record at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Twp.
2. **Munzingen Catholic parish book**, for Heinrich Mayer's baptism around 1796 and Michael Mayer's family. The civil registers in collection L 10 (images free online at the Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg) cover 1810 onward.
3. **Friedrich's emigration file** at the Staatsarchiv Freiburg, plus passenger lists for Le Havre and Antwerp to New York, 1867–68.
4. **Joseph Heizler's death entry** at Munzingen, 1815–34. It would settle whether the Heitzler and Begelspacher gamekeeper line is yours.
5. **Pennsylvania death certificates:**
   - Addison Pringle, 1943, #82141
   - Catherine E. Pringle, 1947, #35591
   - Frank J. McGuire, 1958, #83855
   - Anna A. Meier, 1951 (should name her Higgins parents)
6. **Helen Cognetti's death certificate**, and **Frank Cognetti's 1942 WWII draft card.** These would prove the Ferlaino link and give Frank's Dasà birth date.
7. **Jacobus's articles** in *The American Genealogist*, vols. 12–13, read directly to finalize the Brewster removal.
8. **The Cozes and Moëze Protestant registers**, online at the Charente-Maritime archives. They would give the Lamoureux, Mersereau and Masse baptisms and marriages.
`````

## 3. People

### How this section is organised

- Each person is one JSON object in its own fence, under a heading that gives the full name and birth year.
- **3.1** covers John and his parents. These are living people, and their entries are limited to what the project files record.
- **3.2 to 3.5** follow the four ancestral groups, each running from John's grandparents upward and then listing collateral and notable relatives:
  - **3.2** Meier and its German, McGuire and Higgins lines.
  - **3.3** Pringle, Heffernan and the other Pennsylvania lines, with their Irish and French Huguenot roots.
  - **3.4** The colonial Long Island and English lines above Keturah Tuttle.
  - **3.5** The Italian lines.
- **Disproven people stay in.** People the research removed or disproved still appear, with confidence `unverified` and a reason. The Ancestry tree still shows them, and a future reader needs to know why they were taken out.

By his own account in the 1910 census he immigrated in 1868; the family crossed together (Friedrich, Maria and four small children) between Nov 1866 and Sept 1869; ship and port not found. He appears as 'Henry, 4, Baden' in the 1870 census (Hazleton East Ward, 8 Jun 1870, 'Meyer' household) and 'Henry, 14, son, at school, born Baden' in 1880 ('Myer' household, Hazleton East Ward). On 10 Feb 1892 a licence was issued (Luzerne Orphans' Court marriage docket No. 11054) for Henry J. Meier, born in Germany 15 Nov 1866, residing in Hazleton, moulder, not previously married, and Annie A. Higgins, born New Philadelphia, PA, 2 Oct 1867, residing in Hazleton; they married 1 Mar 1892 at Hazleton (officiant read as 'Rev. Nich. Fo[rve?]' in the Meier notes and 'Rev. Nich. Gow…' in the Irish/PA notes). This docket is the first record spelling the name 'Meier' — written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen it. Sons Fred (1892) and Henry Jr. (1894) were born in Hazleton; Mary (1897) and Madeline (1900) in Wilkes-Barre (Ward 16, 1897–1900, FS tree); the family was in Tamaqua, Schuylkill Co. c.1903–06 (William b. c.1904; Joseph John b. 30 Jun 1906), near Anna's birthplace. In 1910 (Wilkes-Barre Ward 14, ED 158, sheet 20B, 28 Apr 1910, 14 Mill Street, dwelling 376, family 388) he was Henry J. Meier, head, 43, married 19 years, born Germany, both parents born Germany, immigrated 1868, citizenship 'Pa' (first papers only), moulder in a moulding shop, renting; Annie 42 had borne 7 children, 6 living. In 1920 (Ward 15, ED 262, sheet 6A, 7–8 Jan 1920, 298 Barney St, renting) he was 53, molder at an iron works — but this sheet gives his birthplace as 'New York' (informant error; every other record says Germany/Baden); son Henry Jr. lived next door at 296 Barney. In 1926 he was 'Henry', moulder, of Wilkes-Barre (William's application, which wrongly says born 'Penna.'). In 1940 (Ward 15, ED 40-330, sheet 3B, 3 Apr 1940, 16 Barney Street, owned, worth $3,000; same house in 1935) he was 'Meyer, Henry J., 72, born Germany, naturalized (\"Na\"), moulder at an iron works', with Anna A. (72), Mary C. (42) and Joseph J. (33). The citizenship change from 'Pa' (1910) to 'Na' (1940) implies his own naturalization between 1910 and 1940 (papers not found). He died, per the FamilySearch tree LTHM-1XV citing the Find a Grave index (QVG4-98K8), in Dec 1940 in Wilkes-Barre and was buried at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Township. He is NOT in the PA death index for 1939, 1940 or 1941 under Soundex M600 (Meier/Meyer/Maier/Mayer/Moore) as Henry or Harry in Luzerne (the only 1940 'Henry J Meyer' is in Erie, county 25, d. 18 Nov 1940, p.1426), nor in the NYS (ex-NYC) index 1931–71 at a fitting age; no Henry/Harry Meier in the Wilkes-Barre newspaper death lists 1929–40 and 1945. Possible explanations: a late-filed or misspelled certificate (Heinrich, Mier), or the tree's '1940' merged with Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick), 47, d. 9 Feb 1940 Wilkes-Barre. Two Long Island Henry Meier deaths (Huntington 21 Jul 1931, cert. 44888; Hempstead 24 May 1937, cert. 34005) were flagged as leads before the 1940 census proved him alive on 3 Apr 1940 — they cannot be him. A FamilySearch 'Henry Higgins (1866–1940)' (MWTJ-M9C) with identical dates is an unrelated man born in Bethnal Green, London, buried in Outremont, Quebec.",

### 3.3 Pringle, Heffernan and the Pennsylvania lines (with Irish, Palatine German and French Huguenot roots)

Group prefix `pa`. Pringle/Prindle, Heffernan, Connole, Boney, Ryan, Quigley, Dwyer, Scott, Watson, Croup/Grub, Christmann, Young/Jung, Doll, Dietz, Schuch, Lampert, Lamoreaux/Lamoureux (with the Huguenot La Tour, Masse, Mersereau, Dubois), Ives, Davenport. Ordered from John's great-grandmother Florence Pringle upward by generation, then tree-only/disproven entries, then collateral relatives. Generation numbers: John = 0, Florence = 3.

```json
  "summary": "John's 4th-great-grandfather; a coal miner at Mardyke in the Slieveardagh coalfield of Tipperary who died in Ireland before his widow and sons emigrated.",
  "bio": "Thomas Heffernan was baptized at Gortnahoe on 10 Sep 1808, son of Humphrey Heffernan, 'a miner living at Lickfin', and Anastasia Ryan. He married Catherine Boney at Gortnahoe on 3 Feb 1833 and lived at Mardyke, where he was a miner (Dwyer, Branch 4). Mardyke and Lickfinn were collieries in the Slieveardagh coalfield; the Mining Company of Ireland opened its Mardyke mine in 1824 with a Cornish engine and 25 workers' cottages. His children were Jude (bapt. 14 Jul 1839), Andrew Humphrey (bapt. 3 Apr 1842), Richard (bapt. 22 Dec 1844), Catherine (bapt. 6 Feb 1848) and John (bapt. 29 Aug 1852). He died in Ireland, probably between 1852 and about 1864; his son Andrew's obituary mentions only 'his mother and brothers' coming to America. His brother Richard married Catherine's (possible) sister Anastasia Boney; his brothers James and Patrick were transported to New South Wales after the 1834 Ballynonty killing. TREE CORRECTION: Johnny's tree shows Andrew's father as 'Thomas Heffernan 1791-Deceased' (with an obituary-clipping image), son of Patrick Heffernan (1763-1871) and Catherine Neagle (1770). In Dwyer the Thomas baptized in 1791 is Thomas 'of Lanespark' (Branch 1), son of Patrick and Catherine Neagle, who married Catherine Shelly in 1831 - a different man. Dwyer found no proven link between the Patrick/Neagle family and the Humphrey/Ryan family.",
```

```json
  "bio": "Thomas F. Heffernan (10 Mar 1871 - 28 Feb 1951) taught three years in the Plymouth schools, then worked 13 years at the Wilkes-Barre Record. He was assistant county treasurer in 1901 and postmaster of Wilkes-Barre 1907-16 (8 years 11 months), appointed by Theodore Roosevelt in 1907 and reappointed by Taft in 1911. With John A. Hourigan he turned the Morning News into the Evening News (1909). In 1913 he bought the Sunday Independent from John J. Maloney and incorporated it in 1915 with his brothers John V. and George P.; net circulation was 18,777 per issue in 1926 and about 22,000 by 1929, as 'the only Sunday journal' in the valley. Republican; trustee of Mercy Hospital; director of the Wilkes-Barre Deposit & Savings Bank. He married Louise Easen (b. England) at Mauch Chunk in 1900; one son, Thomas E. (b. 1902). Buried Fern Knoll Cemetery, Dallas. The family still ran the Sunday Independent in the 1960s-70s, including through the 1972 and 1978-79 Wilkes-Barre newspaper strikes. The paper's 1913-1958 run is digitized by the Osterhout Free Library on POWER Library. Dwyer credits a portrait of him to Prominent Men, Wilkes-Barre (1906).",
```

### 3.4 Colonial Long Island, New England and English lines

**Colonial group: people (Long Island / New England / English ancestry above Keturah Tuttle).**

Generation numbers below count up from John (gen 0): gen 8 = Thomas Lamoreaux & Keturah Tuttle (6th-great-grandparents, handled by another group); gen 9 = 7th-great-grandparents; gen 10 = 8th; gen 11 = 9th; gen 12 = 10th; gen 13 = 11th; gen 14 = 12th; gen 15 = 13th; gen 16 = 14th-great-grandparents. Path from John: John → Thomas F. Meier (b. 1959) → James C. Meier (b. 1928) → Florence L. Pringle (b. 1903) → Addison F. Pringle (b. 1868) → Andrew G. Pringle (b. 1836) → James Pringle (b. 1798) → Martha Lamoreaux (b. ABT 1771) → Keturah Tuttle (b. 1755) → the people below.

**Whole-branch caveat.** Every ancestor in this file depends on Keturah Tuttle being the daughter of John Tuthill and Temperance Smith (probable). The Smith, Thompson, Topping, Hammond and Paine ancestors further depend on Temperance being the daughter of James Smith & Jerusha Topping (probable). The Tuthill, Wells, Browne, Salmon and Horton ancestors further depend on John Tuthill being the son of James Tuthill & Rachel Browne (probable, strengthened in Round 3).

Austin Smith; Austin, Francis and Jeremiah are exactly the sons of James Smith & Jerusha Topping, i.e. Temperance's brothers. The 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct were signed by 'Thomas Lamoureux' and 'James Tuttle' (probably John's son James, b. 1753). The 'Capt.' title: S. W. Eager, Outline History of Orange County (1846), pp. 527–529, lists 'Capt. J. Tuthill' among Cornwall precinct officers, records that in 1769 the justices cancelled the indenture of apprentice James Simmons 'by the ill-treatment of his master, John Tuthill', and names a 'Capt. Tuthill' on a 1788 committee (too late for a John who died c.1770; possibly son John b. 1753). Ruttenber also lists 'Clove Co.—1775—Jonathan Tuthill, captain.' The deep-dive report found 'no evidence of the title'. The Hauppauge report found no trace of John or Temperance in Smithtown records and noted that the 23 Nov 1752 Smithtown wedding came from an unsourced online tree (My Maine Heritage); Round 2 then found it in Alva Tuttle (1968). If Temperance was raised in Moriches, the couple most plausibly lived in Brookhaven before moving to Orange County; a possible migration vehicle is Rev. Abner Reeve's 1763 removal 'with a company of emigrants' from Moriches to Blooming Grove (possible). The tree had merged him with a James M. Tuthill & Hannah S. Reeve parentage (wrong: that couple is Joshua Tuthill & Hannah Reeve).",

#### Collateral relatives (Keturah's uncles and siblings, Tuthill and Smith kin)

Relationship rule used throughout: J = John's generations up to the shared ancestor (Bull Smith 12; Job Smith 11; John Thompson 12; John Tuthill 1635 12; William Wells 12; John Tuthill Jr. 11; William Hammond 13; Capt. Thomas Topping 13; Francis Brewster 13), C = cousin's generations below it; cousin degree = min(J, C) − 1, removed = |J − C|. Every relationship assumes the two probable links above Keturah (Temperance → James Smith & Jerusha Topping; John Tuthill → James Tuthill & Rachel Browne).

## 4. Family lines and lineage

### 4.0 Overview and surname index

**John's four grandparents**, each the gateway to a group of lines:

| Grandparent | Group | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| James C. Meier (1928–2008) | Paternal grandfather | The Meier line goes back through German Munzingen. Through his mother Florence L. Pringle, the Pringle line opens the Pennsylvania, Irish, Huguenot, Palatine and colonial Long Island lines. |
| Kathryn F. McGuire (1930–1970) | Paternal grandmother | McGuire, McAvoy, Murphy and Jones (Irish and Welsh-American, Pennsylvania). |
| John T. Petriello (b. 1933) | Maternal grandfather | Petriello (Guardia Lombardi) and Gianetta (Bisaccia), both in Avellino. |
| Mary Cognetti (b. 1933) | Maternal grandmother | Cognetti (Dasà, Vibo Valentia) and Ferlaino/Fiorillo/Colosimo (San Mango d'Aquino, Catanzaro). |

| McGuire | 4.1 | John → Thomas F. → Kathryn F. McGuire → Francis J. McGuire → James McGuire → Edward McGuire |

### 4.1 Meier, McGuire and German lines

Generation key used throughout: John (b. 1992) → Thomas F. Meier (b. 1959, living) → **James C. Meier (1928) & Kathryn F. McGuire (1930)** (grandparents) → William F. Meier (c.1904) (great-grandfather) → Henry J. Meier (1866) (2nd great) → Friedrich Mayer (1835) & Maria Anna Birkenmayer (1837) (3rd great) → Heinrich Mayer & Juliana Senn / Servatius Birkenmayer & Agatha Heizler (4th great) → Michael Mayer, Juliana Senn the elder / Johann Ev. Birkenmayer & Magdalena Erb / Joseph Heizler & M. Anna Federer (5th great).

Florence Louise Pringle (William F. Meier's wife, John's great-grandmother) belongs to the Pennsylvania group and is not covered here.

Status labels: confirmed / probable / possible (speculative, lead) / unverified (tree-only or disproven).

#### Meier line (Mayer of Munzingen)

**Path from John:** John → Thomas F. Meier → James C. Meier → William F. Meier → Henry J. Meier → Friedrich Mayer ("Freiderich Meier") → Heinrich ("Henericus") Mayer → Michael Mayer.

**Summary.** This is John's direct paternal surname line. It is now proven generation by generation: US census pages and marriage applications cover the American links, and the original Munzingen civil-register duplicates (Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg, Staatsarchiv Freiburg, L 10 Nr. 1590 for 1810–39 and L 10 Nr. 1591 for 1840–70) cover the German ones. The family came from **Munzingen**, a Tuniberg wine village about 10 km south-west of Freiburg im Breisgau in Baden, today part of the city of Freiburg. It was **not** Kirchzarten. The Ancestry tree and the earlier reports had assumed Kirchzarten because they thought the wife's family came from there; neither side has any record tie to Kirchzarten.

**Origins.** Michael Mayer was a citizen (Bürger) and carpenter (Zimmermann) of Munzingen; his wife and dates are unknown. His son Heinrich (b. c.1796), a mason and later a master mason, married the orphan Juliana Senn (b. c.1798, the illegitimate daughter of Juliana Senn) on 16 Oct 1820 and was "married with house No. 68". They had at least ten children, 1821–1840. Friedrich (b. 2 Mar 1835), also a mason and a Munzingen citizen, married Maria Anna Birkenmaier on 20 Oct 1862. Four generations worked in the building trades: Michael was a carpenter, Heinrich a mason, Friedrich a stone mason, and Henry an iron moulder.

**Emigration.** Friedrich, Maria and four small children (Friedrich b. 1862, Franziska b. 1863, Maria b. 1865 and Heinrich/Henry b. 1866) emigrated between Nov 1866 and Sept 1869. The most likely year is **1868**, which Henry himself reported in the 1910 census; the other children's census entries give 1867 or 1868, and Clarissa was born in Pennsylvania about Sept 1869. The ship and port have not been found. The Bremen Deutsche Auswanderer-Datenbank has no matching family group for 1866–69, so Le Havre or Antwerp is likely. No emigration note was found in the margins of the 1835 or 1862 entries. By June 1870 they were in Hazleton's East Ward, Luzerne Co., PA, where Friedrich worked as a stone mason; his neighbour Anthony Werner was another Baden stone mason. Henry moved through Hazleton (1880–94), Wilkes-Barre Ward 16 (1897–1900), Tamaqua, Schuylkill Co. (c.1903–06) and then Wilkes-Barre (14 Mill St 1910, 298 Barney St 1920, 16 Barney St 1926–40). William was a coal-company clerk and supervisor in Wilkes-Barre (55 Cedar St, 1930–50). James died in Levittown, Bucks Co., PA, in 2008, the first record of the family outside the coal region.

**Spelling history: Mayer → Meier.** There was no formal name change; the spelling drifted with whoever wrote it down.
- The Munzingen registers write **Mayer** throughout, 1820–1862: the 1820 marriage of "Henericus Mayer", the 1821 and 1835 baptisms, and the 1862 marriage of "Friedrich Mayer". Latin and FamilySearch index forms include "Henricus Mayer".
- The 1870 US census has "**Meyer**, Frederick".
- The 1880 census has "**Myer**, Friedrich" ("Fredrick Myer").
- The 1892 Luzerne marriage docket No. 11054 for Henry J. Meier is the **first "Meier"**. A clerk wrote it, so Henry may not have chosen the spelling.
- The PA death indexes have "Meier" for Mary A. (1911) and Frederick (1913).
- From 1910 on the spelling is consistently **Meier**: the 1910 and 1920 censuses, the 1926 marriage application, the 1930 and 1950 censuses, and the 1963 death index. The one exception is "**Meyer**, Henry J." in the 1940 census.
- The Ancestry tree shows "Henry J MEIER MY…" and "Henery Meier", and "Henery" comes from the Latin-style "Henericus" in the 1820 entry.
- The Birkenmayer name varies in the same way: Birkenmayer (1836, 1837, 1842), Birkenmaier (1853, 1862), "Bergenmyer" (1880 census), and "Berkmeier" (Find a Grave index).

**Certainty per link**

| Link | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| John → Thomas F. Meier → James C. Meier | Confirmed (John's own tree and the Bull Smith PDF; living, see section 3.1) | — |
| James C. Meier son of William F. Meier & Florence L. Pringle | **Confirmed** | 1930 census (ED 40-261, 23B) and 1950 census (ED 40-102, sheet 2, "James C"); Ancestry birth-index snippet b. 13 Jul 1928 names parents (probable) |
| William F. Meier son of Henry J. Meier & Anna Higgins | **Confirmed** | 1926 marriage application No. 10768 (father Henry, moulder; mother Anna Higgins; born Tamaqua); 1910 and 1920 censuses |
| Henry J. Meier son of Friedrich Mayer & Maria Anna Birkenmayer | **Confirmed** | 1870 census (Henry 4, Baden) and 1880 census (Henry 14, son, born Baden); the 1892 docket's birth date 15 Nov 1866 matches the tree; FS tree LTHM-1XV |
| Friedrich Mayer b. 2 Mar 1835 Munzingen, son of Heinrich Mayer & Juliana Senn | **Confirmed** | L 10 Nr. 1590 births 1835 No. 10 (plink 5-480946-440); 1862 marriage (plink 5-480947-440) |
| Hazleton Frederick Meier = Munzingen Friedrich Mayer | **Confirmed** | Name, age, Baden birth, wife Maria Anna/Annie b. 1837, and son Henry b. 1866 all match; brother-in-law "Bergenmyer" in 1880 |
| Heinrich Mayer son of Michael Mayer | **Confirmed** | 1820 marriage, L 10 Nr. 1590 marriages 1820 No. 3 (plink 5-480946-215) |
| Juliana Senn daughter of Juliana Senn (elder) | **Confirmed** | 1820 marriage |
| Michael Mayer's wife, parents and dates | Unknown | Not in the 1820 entry; needs the death registers 1810–39 or the parish book |
| Kirchzarten origin (tree/earlier reports) | **Disproven** | No record tie; Dreisamtal DB negative |

**Dates still weak:** James's birth and death (index snippets only); William's birth year (1904 vs 1905); Henry's death (FS: Dec 1940, Wilkes-Barre, St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Twp.; not in the PA index 1939–41); Heinrich's birth c.1796 and death after Oct 1862.

**Collaterals.**
- Henry's ten siblings: Frederick (1862–1915), Frances (1863–1928), Mary (1865–1938), Clarissa (1869), Elizabeth (1872–1945), Theresa (1872–1933), Anna J. (1875–1962), Agatha (1877–1949), Sophia Gertrude (1880–1909) and John Joseph (1883–1966).
- William's siblings: Fred Aloysius (1892–1966), Henry James Jr. (1894–1957), Mary C. (1897–1962), Madeline Edelberta (1900–1995) and Joseph John (1906–1970).
- James's siblings: William F. Jr. (1927–2004) and Barbara Ann (1935–2021). A possible infant, Florence Irene, had a funeral notice in 1933.
- Friedrich's siblings: Maria Anna Creszentia (1821–1872, m. Joseph Wenz 1857), Anton Heinrich Gallus (1822), Stephan (1823), Remigius (1826–1845), Sophie (1831), Karl (1832), Carolina (1833–1857), Johann Baptist Alois (1838–1857) and Pauline (1840, m. Joseph Spinner).
- Possible kin in the earlier generation: the Munzingen masons Anton Mayer and Joseph Mayer, who were godparents in 1821.

#### Senn line

**Path from John:** John → Thomas → James C. → William F. → Henry J. → Friedrich Mayer → **Juliana Senn (b. c.1798)** → **Juliana Senn the elder** (d. before 1820).

**Summary.** Both women were of Munzingen. The younger Juliana was born illegitimately, about 1798, and was "parentless" when she married Heinrich Mayer in 1820. Her father is unknown. FamilySearch index spellings include "Julianna Sann". The German-origins reader read the mother's surname in Friedrich's 1835 baptism as "B[onn?]" under an ink blot, but "Senn" is preferred because the 1820 and 1862 originals say Senn. The Ancestry tree shows Henery Meier's wife only as "Ven Known Meier", meaning unknown.

| Link | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Friedrich's mother = Juliana Senn | **Confirmed** | 1835 birth, 1862 marriage, 1857 sibling marriage index |
| Juliana Senn daughter of Juliana Senn (illegitimate) | **Confirmed** | 1820 marriage |
| Earlier Senn ancestry | Unknown | Munzingen parish book before 1810 |

#### Birkenmayer line (Birkenmaier / Birkenmeier)

**Path from John:** John → Thomas → James C. → William F. → Henry J. → **Maria Anna Birkenmayer (1837)** → **Servatius Birkenmayer (1807)** → **Johann Evangelist Birkenmayer (1771)** → (tree) Matthias Birkenmayer (1739–1803) & Caecilia Hohler (1752) → (tree) Stephan Birkenmaier (1694–1768).

**Origins.** The family was established in **Munzingen**, not the Dreisamtal. Records there include:
- Johann Ev. Birkenmayer (10 Jan 1771 – 17 Dec 1844), a widower and day labourer. In 1836 his title reads "herrschaftl. Waibel[?]", perhaps a seigneurial bailiff or beadle.
- His wife Magdalena Erb, who had died by 1836 (the tree gives 1771–1829).
- Their son Servatius (b. 4 May 1807, or 1806 by his death age; d. 19 Apr 1853), a master glazier and joiner/cabinetmaker and a citizen of Munzingen. He married (Maria) Agatha Heizler on 17 Oct 1836 (the FS index says 27 Oct).
- Seven children: Maria Anna (29 Mar 1837), Rosa (1839, died 1839), Joseph (15 Mar 1842), Rosa (1844–45), Karolina (1846–69), Gabriel E. (20 Jan 1849) and Heinrich (1852–53).

Other Munzingen Birkenmaiers whose relationship to this family is not worked out:
- Johannes Birkenmayer, father of Maria Anna (1810–1865), who married Salesius Schuhmacher.
- Johann Birkenmeier (b. 1808), illegitimate son of Walburga Birkenberger, a master mason in Basel. His daughter Agatha Carolina died in Basel in 1844.
- Infant deaths in 1832.
- The mason Anton Birkenmaier, whose wife was née Scherer.
- A Joseph Birkenmaier who was a marriage witness in 1810.

**Emigration.**
- Maria Anna went to Hazleton with her husband in about 1868.
- Her brother Gabriel lived with them in 1880 (as "Gabriel Bergenmyer", 29, gardener) and later went to Sandusky, Ohio, where he died 2 Dec 1896.
- Her brother Joseph also went to Sandusky and died there 3 Nov 1904 (identity probable, from the Ancestry index).
- Munzingen had an emigrant pipeline to northern Ohio: the village chronicle lists Franz Michel, who left in 1854 and is "assumed to be in Ohio", and Rosalia Dämpfle (b. 1829 Munzingen) died in 1904 at Sherman, Huron Co., OH.

**How the line was found.** Round 1 found no Servatius anywhere. Round 2 established that the Kirchzarten parish database (about 30,000 people) has no Servatius, no Johann E., no Erb and no Hohler. It then found an Ancestry index snippet naming "Servatius Birkenmayer & Agatha Heitzler" as parents of Joseph Birkenmeier, b. 15 Mar 1842 "Münzingen", d. Sandusky 1904. Round 3 read the Munzingen originals and confirmed the line.

#### Heizler / Heitzler line (Kageneck gamekeepers)

**Path from John:** John → … → Maria Anna Birkenmayer → **Agatha Heizler (b. 26 Jun 1813 Munzingen)** → **Joseph Heizler**, herrschaftlicher Jäger (d. 1815–35) → (probable) **Jakob/Jacob Heitzler** (c.1740–1806, Kageneck gamekeeper in Unteribental) & Catharina Begelspacher → (tree) Martinus [= Mathias] Heitzler (1699–1728) & Othilia Schirk → (tree) Andreas Haizler (1665).

**Origins.** The Heitzlers were gamekeepers and forest wardens for the **Counts of Kageneck**.
- The Kagenecks held Munzingen from the mid-17th century and built its Schloss in 1672.
- They acquired **Stegen in 1702**, with the lordship over the Ibental, a side valley east of Freiburg in the Dreisamtal.
- The Dreisamtal database calls Jakob Heitzler "Kageneck'scher Jäger in Unteribental, Waldhüter" and records his part in a 1789 lawsuit. His wife Katharina Begelspacher's father was also a Kageneck gamekeeper.
- Agatha's father **Joseph Heizler** was the "herrschaftlicher Jäger" (seigneurial gamekeeper) at Munzingen. He married M. Anna Federer of Munzingen there on 26 Dec 1799 (FS tree event).
- Joseph and M. Anna's recorded children are Friedrich (8 Mar 1809), Agatha (26 Jun 1813) and Veronica (d. 29 Apr 1815, of measles). Joseph was alive in 1815 and dead by Oct 1835.
- That a Kageneck gamekeeper's son should serve as the Kagenecks' gamekeeper at their Munzingen seat is how an Ibental gamekeeping family would end up in Munzingen.

**The history of the question:**
- **The tree** had "Maria A Heitzler 1813–1867", daughter of Joseph Heitzler 1773–1825 and Maria Anna Federer 1772–1844, and Joseph as the son of Jacob(us) Heitzler (d. 1806) and Catharina Begelspacher (d. 1796).
- **The deep-dive and round 2** found no Joseph among Jakob's recorded children (Andreas 1764, Agathe 1771, Franziska 1779, Jakob 1781) and proposed three rival candidates for the 1813 woman:
  - **A.** Maria Anna Heitzler, b. 8 Apr 1813 Unteribental, daughter of the Ibental schoolteacher Joseph Heitzler (1765–1828) and Maria Pfister. She married J. G. Gremmelspacher in 1855.
  - **C.** The Wehrlehof family of Joseph Heitzler × Maria Rombach, in Oberried-Vörlinsbach.
  - **D.** "Agatha Heitzler", from the Ancestry snippet.
- **Round 3 settled it:** the wife was (Maria) **Agatha** Heizler, daughter of Joseph Heizler & M. Anna Federer of Munzingen. Candidates A and C are **ruled out**. The Stegen "Agatha Heitzler c.1810" (daughter of Andreas Heitzler & Agatha Schlegel) is a different woman, probably a first cousin.
- **Joseph's parentage has been upgraded to probable.** Jakob's recorded children leave gaps (1765–70 and 1772–78) where a Joseph b. c.1773 fits, and Agatha's name repeats Jakob's daughter Agathe (b. 1771).

| Agatha daughter of Joseph Heizler (gamekeeper) & M. Anna Federer | **Confirmed** | 1836 marriage (plink 5-480946-464); brother Friedrich's 1835 marriage (plink 5-480946-450) |
| Joseph Heizler son of Jakob Heitzler & Catharina Begelspacher | **Probable** | Both were Kageneck gamekeepers; gap in Jakob's children; Kageneck Munzingen–Ibental link. No record names Joseph's parents |
| Jakob son of "Martinus" (Mathias) Heitzler & Othilia Schirk | **Possible/unverified** | Tree only. GEDBAS has Mathias Haizler × Ottilia Schirk at the Wehrlehof in 1723–24 (children Christian and Eva, 1724). The tree's 1728 deaths for both would make a c.1740 child impossible, and they are unsupported. Round 3 calls the Wehrlehof/Schirk branch "speculative: no longer Johnny's" |

**Notable collaterals (only proven kin if the probable link holds):**
- Andreas Heitzler (1764–1836), Vogt (village headman) of Unteribental in 1813, who built the "Jägerhäusle" in 1801.
- Jakob (1781–1847), hunter and tailor, who owned house No. 36 in Oberbirken.
- The elder Josef Heitzler, "Bauer und Kageneck'scher Jäger in Stegen", who bought the Jägerhof in 1751 and married Katharina Schlupf. His exact relation to Jakob is not shown.
- Josef Heitzler "vom Jägerhof", Bürgermeister of Unteribental 1919–24. He descends from the elder Josef through the teacher line, so he is the same clan but not a proven cousin now that candidate A is ruled out.

#### Begelspacher line (with Schlemm…, Lickert, Wiederle)

**Path from John:** John → … → Agatha Heizler → Joseph Heizler → (probable) Catharina Begelspacher (d. 1796, tree) → (tree) **Joseph Begelspacher (b. 3 Mar 1704)** & Maria Schlemm… → **Martin Begelspacher (1656–1711)** & **Magdalena Lickert** (1664, tree) → **Matthias Begelspacher (b. 1 Feb 1630 Burg)** & **Barbara Wiederle (b. 25 Nov 1629 Weilersbach, d. 11 Jan 1693)**. - Martin was the "Jägerhofbauer", farmer of the Jägerhof in Unteribental, and married Magdalena Lickert about 1700.
- Josef was born 3 Mar 1704.
- The Jägerhof was bought by the gamekeeper Josef Heitzler in 1751. If it is the same farm, the Begelspachers and Heitzlers lived on the same homestead two generations apart.

#### Croup / Grub / Croop line (Palatine German)

**Path:** … → Andrew G. Pringle → **Elizabeth Croup** (1802–1895) → **Frederick Croup/Grub** (c.1767–1841) → **Johann Andreas Grub** (1727–1792) → Johann Nickel Grub (c.1694–1763) → Johann Peter Grub (1655–1739) → Caspar Grub (1616–1671) → Christmann Grub of Oberbrombach → Hanns Grub.

**Origins.** **Jettenbach**, Kusel district, Duchy of Palatinate-Zweibrücken (today Rhineland-Palatinate), Lutheran; earlier at **Berschweiler bei Kirn** and **Oberbrombach/Niederbrombach** (Birkenfeld district), moving to Jettenbach in the generations after the Thirty Years' War. Ulmet (the Dolls) is about 5 km away; Lauterecken and Glan-Münchweiler are in the same Kusel–Glan uplands.

**Emigration.** Andreas probably on the *Phoenix*, Philadelphia, 1 Oct 1754 (Strassburger List 222; a "Johannes Young/Jung" heads the same list). Settled Williams Twp (1759), Bethlehem Twp (1772), Easton (1773), Forks Twp, Northampton Co. (by 1781; 100 acres 1788, beside the Delaware north of Easton near today's Lafayette College). Frederick moved to the Susquehanna at Hunlock's Creek/Nanticoke about 1799–1800 (Bradsby says "soon after" 1790). The family were farmers and landowners; the Croop sawmills and later Croop's Glen amusement park belong to nephew John Croop's line (with the Sorbers).

#### Lamoreaux / Lamoureux line (Huguenot)

**Path:** John → … → Florence → Addison → Andrew G. → James Pringle → Samuel Pringle × **Martha Lamoreaux** (c.1770–72) → **Ensign Thomas Lamoreaux** (c.1745–1829) → **Jean (John) Lamoreaux** (1723–1809) → **Daniel Lamoureux** (b. Bristol 1695) → **André Lamoureux** (b. Cozes 1663) → Daniel Lamoureux & Marie Touchay of Cozes → Jean Lamoureux of Cozes (fl. before 1656).

**Origins.** Huguenots of **Saintonge** (modern Charente-Maritime): André was a shipmaster and Gironde pilot "cy-devant de Meche en Xaintonge" = **Meschers-sur-Gironde** (confirmed); baptized at the Reformed parish of **Cozes**, ~8 km inland (probable). **Not La Rochelle** (no record; confusion from the Mersereau in-law Suzanne Doucinet "de la ville de la Rochelle"). The "three brothers who came direct from France in 1770–72" tradition is false.

**Migration.** Meschers → **Bristol** 1689–95 (French Church; denization 22 Jun 1694) → **New York City** by 15 May 1700 (1703 census, West Ward) → Daniel to New Rochelle, Bedford, Philipse Precinct near Davenport's Corners (Philipstown) → Jean to Goshen precinct / **Monroe, Orange Co., NY** → Thomas to Woodbury Clove/Cornwall → **Plymouth, PA (spring 1790)** → Jackson Twp (Chase).

Miners in Tipperary; Andrew became a Court House attaché; next generation clerks, postmaster, editors, doctors, a nun and an Army aviator.

#### Smith line (Richard “Bull” Smith of Smithtown)

**Path from John:** trunk → Keturah Tuttle → Temperance Smith (b. ABT 1735) → James Smith (b. 1688) → Job Smith (b. ABT 1647) → Richard “Bull” Smith (b. ABT 1613) & Sarah Hammond.

**Origins.** English origin unknown. Pelletreau (1898): “we know absolutely nothing”; Yorkshire said “by some historians” on insufficient evidence; “Myreshaw, Bradford” unsourced (WikiTree Smith-1208). F. K. Smith (1967): probably the Richard Smith, 22, who sailed 2 Oct 1635 on the *John* of London for St Christophers; probably raised in London (court-hand script). Gloucestershire: disproven (belongs to Richard Smith of Cocumscussoc/Wickford RI, ex-Taunton). Bedfordshire: no source (cross-wiring with Topping). Y-DNA R-b1, SmithConnections NE50, no English match. Tree’s parents Sir Samuel Smith (1575–1618) & Rebecca Buswell (1593–1667), and Rebecca’s mother Margaret Buswell (1550–1612): unsupported, remove.

**Emigration / settlement.** Massachusetts by 1640 (breach-of-promise petition re Sarah Hammond, April 1640) → Southampton (home lot 1640/1643, south end of village, west side of main street) → possibly back to England 1654, returned 1656 on the *Speedwell* with first Quaker missionaries; banished from Southampton → bought Smithtown from Lion Gardiner 1663, patent 1665 → Nissequogue home lots (Jonathan’s, Richard’s, Job’s). James Smith later moved to Moriches; his sons Austin, Francis and Jeremiah, and daughter Temperance, went to Woodbury Clove, Orange Co., NY.

**Tree vs research.** Tree: James F Smith 1688–1740, father “Justice, A Smith” 1649–1726 (+ Elizabeth Thompson 1657–1718), grandfather “Maj R B Sm(y)ith” 1613–1692 + “Sarah F Hammond” 1623–1708. Preferred: James’s father is **Job Smith** (PDF; F. K. Smith “James Smith (Job, Richard)”; Round 1 correction 3f). The 1649 “Justice A Smith” matches Bull Smith’s son Adam (b. 1649). Rival Temperance (daughter of Ebenezer & Anna Smith) ruled out — she married Jonas Platt, d. 1813.

#### Regional summary (Long Island, colonial only, c.1640–1760)

Smithtown/Nissequogue (Bull & Job Smith home lots; James Smith’s 1736 tract on the Hauppauge border); Moriches (James Smith & Jerusha Topping); Southampton, Sagaponack (Sagg), Bridgehampton (Toppings; Bull Smith’s first home lot); Southold, Cutchogue, Mattituck, Oysterponds (William Wells, Tuthills, Brownes, Salmons, Barnabas Horton); Setauket/Brookhaven (John Thompson’s home lot facing the green; James Tuthill’s 1714/1721 land); cousin sites: Gardiner’s Island and East Hampton (Julia Tyler), Sagtikos Manor (Thompsons), Hauppauge (Smith judges), Flushing (Lawrences). Then Orange County, NY: Woodbury Clove, Cornwall Precinct, Goshen, New Windsor, Blooming Grove. No direct colonial ancestor lived in Virginia; Revolutionary service in Virginia: none found.

### 4.4 Italian lines (Petriello, Gianetta, Cognetti, Ferlaino, Fiorillo, Colosimo)

#### Maternal Italian lines: overview

All of John's maternal (Petriello-side) ancestry is Italian, from two regions and five comuni, and every immigrant line ended up in **Scranton / Dunmore, Lackawanna County, Pennsylvania**:

| Comune (province) | Lines | Scranton/Dunmore colony | Status of origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Guardia Lombardi (Avellino, Campania) | Petriello/Petrillo, Marra, Di Marino, Magnotta, di Leo, Di Biase/DiBiasi, Siconolfi, Carrozzino (and the detached d'Ambrosio/Gialanella/Giordano/Di Vivo/Parisi cluster) | Bunker Hill section of Dunmore / Scranton 10th Ward; St. Rocco's Church (1905) | Confirmed (civil records) |
| Bisaccia (Avellino) | Giannetta/Gianetta, Fede, Macchia(?), Roberto | Dunmore (133 Sand St; Ward 5) | Confirmed |
| Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi (Avellino) | Ferrantino (a foundling's assigned surname) | Dunmore | Confirmed (birthplace); parents unknown |
| Dasà (Vibo Valentia; formerly Catanzaro / Calabria Ultra II) | Cognetta/Cognetti, Cannatello, Malvaso, Croce, Lamanna | Scranton (Ward 2, Philo St) | Confirmed for Giovanni Cognetta; Frank Cognetti's own birthplace unproven |
| San Mango d'Aquino (Catanzaro, Calabria) | Ferlaino, Fiorillo, Colosimo, Marrelli | Providence section, Scranton (1306 Diamond Ave); San Mango d'Aquino Mutual Benefit Society | Confirmed back to c.1808; pre-1800 Fiorillo/Morrello pedigree unsupported |

The Petriello side (John T. Petriello) is wholly Irpinian: Guardia via his father James and Bisaccia/Sant'Angelo via his mother Mollie. The Cognetti side (Mary Cognetti) is wholly Calabrian: Dasà via Frank and San Mango via Helen. No tie to Long Island or Virginia was found for any Italian line.

**No Moraca line appears anywhere in the project files.** The surname Moraca does not occur in the Ancestry-tree transcription, the tree-screenshot details, any of the three round reports, any research notes (round 1, 2 or 3), or John's uploaded reports. (A full-text search of /mnt/project-files for "moraca" returned no hits.) If the family believes there is a Moraca ancestor, it is not yet in the tree or research and would be a new line to investigate.

---

##### Petriello line

**Path from John:** John (b. 1992) → mother Sharon M. Petriello (b. 1960) → John T. Petriello (b. 1933) → James Petriello/Petrillo (1910–1998) → John (Giovanni) Petriello (1869–1939) → Pietro Petriello (c.1837–1901) → Angelo Petriello (d. before 1869) + Lucia Marra.

**Origins:** Guardia Lombardi (Guardia dei Lombardi), province of Avellino, Campania (Irpinia). Petriello is concentrated in Avellino province (paese.app: 2 US arrivals from Guardia 1830–1912; modern Guardia phone directory lists Petriello 6). A New York "Association of Former Citizens of Guardia Lombardi" lists Petriellos among its officers. Name forms: Petriello, Petrillo, Petrello, Patrello used interchangeably in the US; most of John Petriello's children used Petrillo.

**Emigration:** John Petriello made more than one crossing: censuses give immigration 1880 (1910) and 1892 (1920); FS-tree arrival events 1880, 1890, 1892; naturalized 1900. His grocery was open by 1897 (before St. Rocco's was founded in 1905), at 1030 Ash St (1910) and 1028 Bunker Hill (1920), Scranton Ward 10. Family briefly in Pittston (son Charles b. 1906). Round 1's "first arrival c.1889–95" inference was voided when Rocco James (b. 1889) proved to be from another family.

##### Morrello / Guercio / Chiarello / Vecchio / Marsico / Briglio / Fata / Palladino pedigree (flagged unsupported)

**Tree path:** John → … → Carmine Fiorillo (1808) → Domenico G. Fiorillo (1785–1849) + Maria Morrello (1786–1846).
- Domenico G. Fiorillo (1785) → Carmine G. Fiorillo (d. 1797) + [empty] → Domenico G. Fiorillo (d. 1770) + Cecilia Fata Scaff… (1738–1797) → Antonio Fata Tang… (1701–1764) + Fulvia Palladino (1708–1774).
- Maria Morrello → Vincenzo Morrello M… (1759–1836) + Ippolita Guercio N… (1761–1831).
  - Vincenzo → Domenico Morrello M… (1716–1790) + Maria Chiarello (1733–1807); Maria Chiarello → Celio Chiarello (d. 1739) + Giulia Marsico (b. 1712).
  - Ippolita → Nicola Guercio N… (1714–1782) + Cecilia Vecchio (b. 1718); Nicola → Marc'Antonio Guercio (b. 1684) + Anna Briglio (b. 1694).

**Status: unverified / unsupported.** Reasons:
1. San Mango's parish stati delle anime 1674–1804 (ItalianParishRecords.org, 14 years, 309–1,610 people per year) have **0** entries for Fiorillo, Fata, Morrello/Morello, Chiarello, Palladino and Briglio (incl. fuzzy spellings); Domenico G. Fiorillo (1785) + Maria Morrello (1786) should appear in 1800/1804 and do not. Guercio (163), Marsico (68), Vecchio (10), Colosimo (652) and Ferlaino (229) do appear, but not these couples (a San Mango Nicola Guercio b. c.1741–50 married Maria Colosimo — a different man).
2. Carmine Fiorillo's 1860 death act names his mother **Vittoria Marrelli**, not Maria Morrello.
3. Several profiles (Domenico G. Fiorillo 1785, Cecilia Fata, Vincenzo & Domenico Morrello, Maria Chiarello, Nicola Guercio, Cecilia Vecchio, Ippolita Guercio) carry the same coat of arms (black shield, silver rampant lion, crown, wreath), which matches none of 35+ nearby comuni checked; it may be a family/noble arms or copied from another user's tree. Several of these (Fata, Palladino; Carmine & Giuseppina; Leopoldo & Giuseppina) appear as "Potential" (unaccepted hint) cards in the screenshots.
4. Dates of 1684–1738 births can only come from parish registers (comune founded c.1640; parish 1648).

Most likely explanation (Round 2, probable): the pre-1800 pedigree belongs to another comune (perhaps Nocera Terinese, Martirano, Conflenti, Motta Santa Lucia or Cleto — speculative) or was copied from another family's tree. Morrello, Guercio, Chiarello, Palladino, Vecchio and Briglio are not on the modern San Mango surname list.

## 5. Stories

The stories are grouped by family line. Each gives an approximate date, the people involved (name and birth year), the text, and its source. Where a story is family tradition rather than documented history, that is said.

### 5.0 Story from the Drive folder (Claude chat screenshot)

#### "Whisper", the Smithtown Bull statue

- **Approximate date:** the statue was proposed in the early 1900s and installed in Smithtown in 1941. Bull Smith died on 7 Mar 1692.
- **People involved:**
  - Richard "Bull" Smith (b. unknown; estimates are about 1613–1615; the tree shows 1613), John's 10th-great-grandfather.
  - Lawrence Smith Butler (b. unknown), a descendant of Bull Smith.
  - Charles Cary Rumsey (b. unknown), the sculptor.
- **Text:**
  - Theories about Bull Smith's nickname include his stubbornness, and the idea that he issued his own "Smith Bull", like a papal bull, to settle his boundary disputes.
  - Lawrence Smith Butler proposed a bronze bull statue to his friend Charles Cary Rumsey. It sat in the Brooklyn Museum for years before it was installed in Smithtown in 1941. The bull is named "Whisper".
  - For years, local graduating seniors would sneak out and paint one particular part of the bull bright red.
  - The statue stands at the junction of Routes 25 and 25A. Bull Smith actually lived at Nissequogue.
  - The bull-ride legend itself (that Smith won his land by riding a bull around it in a day) is a myth, according to John's uploaded deep-dive report.
- **Source:** the Drive screenshot IMG_7801, a Claude chat answer that listed sources the screenshot does not show; and the uploaded deep-dive report ("The bull-ride story is a myth").

### 5.1 Meier, McGuire and German lines

#### From Mayer to Meier: a name nobody formally changed
- Approximate date: 1820–1940
- People involved: Heinrich Mayer (b. 1796); Friedrich Mayer (b. 1835); Henry J. Meier (b. 1866); William F. Meier (b. 1904)
- Text: The original Munzingen registers write the family name **Mayer** every time, from Heinrich's 1820 marriage (as "Henericus Mayer") through Friedrich's 1835 baptism to his 1862 wedding.
  - **Meyer:** the 1870 Hazleton census-taker wrote "Meyer, Frederick".
  - **Myer:** the 1880 census-taker wrote "Myer, Friedrich".
  - **Meier:** the spelling first appears on Henry J. Meier's 1892 Luzerne marriage docket (No. 11054). A clerk wrote it, so Henry may not have chosen it.
  - From 1910 on, every record says Meier, with one exception: the 1940 census-taker wrote "Meyer, Henry J."

  No formal name change has been found. The tree's odd "Henery Meier" for Friedrich's father echoes the Latin-style "Henericus" of the 1820 entry.
- Source: notes/round3/meier_line.md (1820 marriage, plink 5-480946-215; 1835 birth, 5-480946-440; 1862 marriage, 5-480947-440; 1870, 1880, 1910, 1920, 1940 census images; docket No. 11054); research-thread answer to John's question 6 (section 1.4).

#### Four generations in the building trades
- Approximate date: c.1790–1940
- People involved: Michael Mayer (b. unknown); Heinrich Mayer (b. 1796); Friedrich Mayer (b. 1835); Henry J. Meier (b. 1866)
- Text: Each generation worked in a building trade:
  - Michael was a citizen and carpenter (Zimmermann) of Munzingen.
  - Heinrich was a mason (Maurer), and later a master mason (Maurermeister).
  - Friedrich was a mason in Munzingen and a stone mason in Hazleton in 1870 and 1880.
  - Henry was an iron moulder for nearly 50 years.
- Source: Round 3 report section 2; notes/round3/meier_line.md.

#### Stonemasons from a wine village
- Approximate date: 1672–1870
- People involved: Friedrich Mayer (b. 1835); Anthony Werner (b. c.1819, neighbour, not kin)
- Text: Munzingen sits among the Tuniberg vineyards under the Counts of Kageneck, whose castle (Schloss) there dates from 1672. In Hazleton's East Ward in 1870, Friedrich's next-door neighbour was Anthony Werner, 51, also a stone mason from Baden. That points to a small network of Baden building tradesmen in Hazleton. Friedrich's eldest son Fred was already a coal-mine laborer at 18 in 1880.
- Source: Round 3 report §5; notes/round3/meier_line.md §6 (1870 census p.42; 1880 census ED 137); notes/round2/black_forest.md (Kageneck).

#### A brother-in-law with "fever & ague"
- Approximate date: 11 Jun 1880
- People involved: Gabriel E. Birkenmeier (b. 1849); Friedrich Mayer (b. 1835); Maria Anna Birkenmayer (b. 1837); Joseph Birkenmayer (b. 1842)
- Text: On census day 1880, Gabriel "Bergenmyer", 29, a gardener born in Baden, was living with his sister's family in Hazleton. He was sick with "fever & ague", a malaria-type fever. He later moved to Sandusky, Ohio, where his brother Joseph already lived, and died there in 1896. This census entry is also what proves Maria's maiden name.
- Source: notes/round3/meier_line.md (1880 census, ED 137 p.13); Round 3 report §5.

#### A moulder for fifty years
- Approximate date: 1892–1940
- People involved: Henry J. Meier (b. 1866)
- Text: Henry was a moulder (foundry worker) when he married at 25 in 1892. He was still a "moulder, iron works" at 72 in the April 1940 census, months before he died. He lived at 16 Barney Street, Wilkes-Barre, which he owned; it was valued at $3,000.
- Source: notes/round3/meier_line.md §3, §6; notes/round3/irish_pa.md.

#### The Tamaqua years
- Approximate date: c.1903–1906
- People involved: Henry J. Meier (b. 1866); Anna A. Higgins (b. 1867); William F. Meier (b. 1904); Joseph John Meier (b. 1906)
- Text: Around 1905–06 Henry's family lived in Tamaqua, Schuylkill County, close to Anna's birthplace of New Philadelphia. John's great-grandfather William was born there, and his brother Joseph John was born there on 30 Jun 1906.
