- Text: Theodore Roosevelt is buried in Oyster Bay’s Youngs Memorial Cemetery, on Youngs family land, but he is not a blood relative — and the Youngs ancestry itself is unproven.
- Source: notes/colonial_virginia.md §3d.

#### Stephen Sayre, a cousin who wasn’t
- Approximate date: 1818
- People involved: Stephen Sayre (b. 1736)
- Text: Stephen Sayre, Sheriff of London and Franklin’s agent, died in 1818 “at the residence of his son in Brandon, Virginia”. He would have been John’s 3C9R had the tree’s Sayre line been right; it isn’t.
- Source: notes/colonial_virginia.md §3d, §4 (Banks 1901; *Richmond Enquirer* 10 Dec 1818).

### 5.4 Italian lines (Petriello, Gianetta, Cognetti, Ferlaino, Fiorillo, Colosimo)

#### The two "Marys": how Mollie was mistaken for Mary Cognetti
- Approximate date: 1931–1933 (the people); 2026 (the correction)
- People involved: Carmela "Mollie" Gianetta (b. 1910); Mary Cognetti (b. 1933); James Petriello (b. 1910); John T. Petriello (b. 1933)
- Text: The Ancestry tree showed "Mollie Petriello 1911–" as James Petriello's wife and left it unclear whether Mollie was Mary Cognetti. Round 1 worked out that Mollie (b. 1911) was James's wife, and so John T.'s mother, while Mary Cognetti (b. c.1933) married John T., James's son. The two were probably confused because "Mollie" is a pet form of Mary. Round 2 found James's 1931 marriage license (No. 1107), where the bride is "Mollie Genett", 20, of 133 Sand St, Dunmore, daughter of Frank, a blacksmith, and Angelica née Ferrandino. FamilySearch identifies her as Carmela Gianetta (13 Jul 1910 – 7 Feb 2000); her Social Security entry reads "Mollie C Petriello", where the C is for Carmela.
- Source: Round 1 report correction 3n; notes/italian.md 2.3; Round 2 report 1 and 3e; notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 1 (FS VF76-TJQ, VF76-TJ9, GQ4M-KCR, SSDI JRHQ-NYH)

#### A teenage wedding needing parental consent
- Approximate date: 20 Jun – 12 Jul 1931
- People involved: James Petriello (b. 1910); Carmela "Mollie" Gianetta (b. 1910); John (Giovanni) Petriello (b. 1869); Angelica Ferrantino (b. 1873)
- Text: James and Mollie were both 20, minors under the law of the time, so "John Petrillo" and "Angelina Genett" had to consent on the license. They were married at Dunmore in July 1931 (FamilySearch gives 12 Jul) by Rev. Michael DeLarno.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md section 1 (license No. 1107, image https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/GQWR-TY6/images/i/1/image.jpg)

#### A foundling's name
- Approximate date: c.1873 (birth); 1 Aug 1896 (marriage)
- People involved: Angelica Ferrantino (b. 1873); Frank Giannetta (b. 1869)
- Text: When Angelica married Frank Giannetta at Bisaccia in 1896, the marriage act described her as aged 23, born in Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi and living in Bisaccia, "figlia di padre ignoto e madre ignota": a child of unknown father and unknown mother. She was a foundling. Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi was a district seat with a foundling wheel (ruota), and "Ferrantino" is typical of the surnames the authorities gave to esposti, so the name was probably assigned to her at the wheel. John's great-great-grandmother's real parents are unknown. Her foundling birth act cannot be reached online, because the Antenati registers for Sant'Angelo stop at 1865.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md section 3 and "Town and people facts"; Round 3 report sections 1 and 5 (Bisaccia Matrimoni 1896 act 18, https://antenati.cultura.gov.it/ark:/12657/an_ua445513/5glz731)

#### Shepherds of Bisaccia
- Approximate date: 1867
- People involved: Savino Giannetta (b. 1842); Bartolomeo Fede (b. unknown); Angelamaria Fede (b. 1849)
- Text: Savino Giannetta, who married Angelamaria Fede in 1867, was a pecoraio (shepherd), and so was her father Bartolomeo Fede. That is typical of Bisaccia, an upland grazing town. By the time Savino's son Frank married in 1896, Frank was described as "possidente" (a property owner). In America he worked as a blacksmith.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md 3 and "Town and people facts"; Round 3 report section 5

#### Bisaccia: a castle town of emperors and poets
- Approximate date: Bronze Age – present
- People involved: Frank Giannetta (b. 1869) and the Giannetta/Fede ancestors; town-mates Mario Procaccino (b. 1912) and Franco Arminio (b. 1960)
- Text: Bisaccia was a Bronze Age site. The Oliveto-Cairano culture (9th c. BC) left Iron Age burials there, including the "tomb of the princess". The town appears in the Catalogus Baronum. Frederick II rebuilt the castle c.1250, and the town is associated with the Sicilian School of poetry. Torquato Tasso stayed there in 1588 as a guest of G. B. Manso, and the Pignatelli were dukes from 1600. Earthquakes struck in 1694, 1732, 1930 and 1980. The population fell from about 8,000 (1968) to about 3,400. The patron saint is Sant'Antonio di Padova (13 June). About 916 people left Bisaccia for America between 1830 and 1912, with the peak in 1906, the year the FamilySearch tree says Frank Giannetta came (his own 1920 declaration says 1903). Mario Procaccino, New York City Comptroller and the 1969 Democratic nominee for mayor, was born in Bisaccia, as was the poet Franco Arminio (paesologia of depopulated Irpinia). Neither is known to be kin.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md "Town and people facts" (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisaccia_(Italia)); Round 2 report section 4; notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 6 and 8 (https://paese.app/regioni/campania/avellino/bisaccia)

#### Frank Giannetta crosses on the SS Italia
- Approximate date: c.15 Apr 1903; declaration 12 Jul 1920
- People involved: Frank Giannetta (b. 1869); Angelica Ferrantino (b. 1873)
- Text: Frank Giannetta signed his Declaration of Intention (No. 16537) in the US District Court at Scranton on 12 Jul 1920 as "Frank Gennetti". He was then 50, a laborer living at 133 Sand St, Dunmore, and born 2 May 1869 in "Bisiccio" (Bisaccia). He had sailed from Naples on the SS *Italia* and reached New York around 15 Apr 1903. His last foreign residence was Bisaccia, and his wife Angelina was born in Italy.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md 3 (image https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/LCPG-XKM/images/i/2/image.jpg)

#### The candle-maker of Dasà
- Approximate date: 22 Mar 1855
- People involved: Nicola Cognetta (b. 1804); Mariangela Cannatello (b. 1823); Giovanni Cognetta (b. 1855)
- Text: When Giovanni Cognetta was registered at Dasà in 1855, his father was styled "Mastro Nicola Cognetta", 51, a ceraiuolo (a wax-chandler or candle-maker who made votive and church candles), and his mother "Donna Mariangela Cannatello". The honorifics "Mastro" (master craftsman) and "Donna" mark a family of slightly elevated, artisan status.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md 4 and "Town and people facts"; Round 3 report section 5 (Dasà Nati 1855 act 18, https://antenati.cultura.gov.it/ark:/12657/an_ua37922783/0JPovJv)

#### Dasà: the "wood" town and its Easter Affruntata
- Approximate date: medieval to 1929
- People involved: the Cognetta, Cannatello and Malvaso ancestors
- Text: Dasà's name comes from the Greek *dásos*, "wood". It was once a casale of Arena, a fief of the Culchebret family, and was rebuilt after the 1783 and 1905 earthquakes. Its feast, the 'Ncrinata/Affruntata, falls on Easter Tuesday. Its emigrants went mainly to Stamford, Connecticut, and paid for Dasà's 1929 war memorial.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 3 and 8 (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Das%C3%A0)

#### Guardia Lombardi: a Lombard lookout fort
- Approximate date: 571 – 1980
- People involved: the Petriello, Di Marino and DiBiasi ancestors
- Text: Guardia Lombardi was founded by the Lombards (Longobards) about 571–591 as a *guardia*, a lookout fort of the Gastaldate of Conza. Roger II destroyed it in 1133, and Manfred defeated a papal army there on 30 Oct 1254. Earthquakes struck in 1694 (about 280 dead), 1732 and 1930, and the Irpinia earthquake of 23 Nov 1980 destroyed more than 50% of its buildings. The population fell from 5,508 in 1921 to about 1,700 in 2017. The patron saint is Pope St. Leo IX.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 8 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardia_Lombardi; https://www.earth-prints.org/bitstream/2122/14394/1/geosciences_Porfido_et_al_2020.pdf); Round 2 report section 4

#### The plague of 1656 and Father Di Leo's chapel to St. Rocco
- Approximate date: 1656
- People involved: Fr. Nunzio Di Leo (no proven link); Caterina di Leo (b. unknown) shares the surname
- Text: A plague in 1656 killed 1,110 of Guardia's 1,475 people. Fr. Nunzio Di Leo's will funded a chapel to St. Rocco, the plague saint. The name "di Leo" matches that of Grazia Di Marino's mother, Caterina di Leo. No kinship is proven.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 8 (https://irpiniastories.wordpress.com/2022/08/11/ties-that-remain-celebrating-guardia-lombardi-in-pennsylvania/); Round 2 report section 4

#### St. Rocco's, Dunmore, and John Petriello's grocery
- Approximate date: 1897 – 2010
- People involved: John (Giovanni) Petriello (b. 1869); Maria Antonia DiBiasi (b. 1870)
- Text: "More than one hundred years ago" emigrants from Guardia Lombardi settled the Bunker Hill section of Dunmore. About 40 Guardiese families bought a former Presbyterian church there, and the first Mass was said in October 1905; the cornerstone is in Italian. The first procession was held in August 1906. St. Rocco's became a parish in 1922 and merged into SS. Anthony & Rocco in 2010. Scranton, Dunmore and Guardia are now sister cities; Stephanie Longo of Dunmore, an author of Guardia descent, set up those ties (no known kinship). John Petriello's grocery, already open by 1897 on Ash St and later on Bunker Hill, would have served that early colony, so John and Maria Antonia were among the earliest Guardiese on Bunker Hill. The Guardiese neighbourhood straddles Scranton's 10th Ward and Dunmore. That is why the family appears in Scranton censuses but married and was buried in Dunmore.
- Source: notes/italian.md 2.1; notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 6 and 8 (Irpinia Stories; WNEP https://wnep.com/article/news/local/lackawanna-county/festival-and-feast-of-st-rocco-a-dunmore-tradition/523-cbeab741-2694-4e93-9676-0e421060fa07; We The Italians https://www.wetheitalians.com/news/italians-lackawanna-county-wonderful-community-where-people-love-and-respect-each-other; Facebook https://www.facebook.com/ScrantonDunmoreGuardia/); Round 2 report section 4

#### The grocer of Bunker Hill
- Approximate date: 1897–1931
- People involved: John (Giovanni) Petriello (b. 1869)
- Text: In 1910 John "Petrillo" kept a grocery store on his own account at 1030 Ash Street, in a house he owned with a mortgage. By 1920 he was a "merchant, grocery store" at 1028 Bunker Hill and owned the house free of mortgage. On his son's 1931 license his occupation was "Mdse" (merchandise). His two censuses give different immigration years (1880 and 1892), and his age drifts (35 in 1910, 50 in 1920), which suggests more than one crossing.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 4 (1910 and 1920 census images)

#### Close kin networks in Guardia
- Approximate date: 1855–1906
- People involved: Pietro Petriello (b. 1837); Francesco De Biasi (b. ABT 1829); the Petriello, Marra, Di Marino and De Biasi families
- Text: In Guardia's records the Petriello, Marra, Di Marino and De Biasi families act as witnesses for one another. A Francesco De Biasi, 72, reported Pietro Petriello's death in 1901. A Petriello–Marra–Di Marino web of marriages appears in the 1855 indexes: Pietro's sister Gaetana married in February, and his future wife's half-sister Concetta married a Giuseppe Petriello (son of Carmine and Maria Marra) in December. The allegati to Guardia's 1906 deaths include a death certificate from St. Anthony's Church, Dunmore, PA, for a Guardiese, confirming the Guardia-to-Dunmore migration chain.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md sections 1, 2 and "Town and people facts"

#### Gaetano di Marino's two wives
- Approximate date: before 1855–1876
- People involved: Gaetano di Marino (b. 1796); Maria d'Ambrosio (b. unknown); Caterina di Leo (b. unknown); Grazia Di Marino (b. 1845); Concetta di Marino (b. unknown)
- Text: John's Ancestry tree made Maria d'Ambrosio the mother of Grazia Di Marino, while FamilySearch said Caterina di Leo. Grazia's own death act (1916) settled it: Caterina di Leo. A December 1855 marriage index shows another daughter of Gaetano, Concetta, whose mother was Maria d'Ambrosio. Gaetano evidently married twice, first Maria d'Ambrosio and then Caterina di Leo, and the tree had merged the two wives. As a result the whole D'Ambrosio/Gialanella pedigree drops out of John's direct line.
- Source: notes/round3/italian_origins.md 1; Round 3 report section 3

#### "Farino": how a census clerk hid the Ferlainos
- Approximate date: 2–3 Jan 1920; 1940; 1943; 2008
- People involved: Helen Ferlaino (b. 1894); Giuseppina Fiorillo (b. 1871); Anthony R. Cognetti (b. 1924)
- Text: The 1920 census enumerator wrote the whole Ferlaino household at 1306 Diamond Avenue as "Farino". Two of Helen's sons later gave their mother's maiden name as "Farino" on their marriage licenses (1940, 1943), and Anthony R. Cognetti's 2008 obituary echoed it as "Helen Farina Cognetti". For a while this cast doubt on the tree's Ferlaino line. The address and a boarder named in an independent forum post show the household was the Ferlainos'.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 2; Round 2 report 1 and 3e

#### The Ferlaino boarding house at 1306 Diamond Avenue
- Approximate date: 1910s–1920s
- People involved: Giuseppina Fiorillo (b. 1871); Helen Ferlaino (b. 1894); Frank Cognetti (b. 1891); boarders Antonio Epifano and Angelo Bonacci
- Text: 1306 Diamond Avenue, Scranton, "was the home of the Ferlaino family who took in boarders from San Mango d'Aquino". It was a landing place for newly arrived men from the town. In January 1920 the widowed Josephine (Giuseppina) owned it free of mortgage and lived there with her children Helen, Frank and Raffaela; Helen's husband Frank Cognetti (listed as a "boarder"); three Cognetti grandsons; and boarders Anthony "Bifano" (Antonio Epifano) and Angelo Bonacci. A John Bifano (Epifano) later co-indexed San Mango's parish records with Daniel Lupia.
- Source: notes/italian.md 4 (https://www.italiangenealogy.com/forum/topic/26645); notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 2 and 7; Round 2 report section 4

#### A grandson named Leopold
- Approximate date: 19 May 1929
- People involved: Leo S. Cognetti (b. 1929); Leopoldo Ferlaino (b. 1871)
- Text: Helen's son born in 1929 was named Leopold Salvatore ("Leopoldo" in the 1930 census), apparently for her father Leopoldo Ferlaino, who had died in 1915. This is one of the clues that Helen was a Ferlaino. The Ancestry tree misreads his name as "Levyso" (1930–Living), and FamilySearch has a duplicate "Leupo". He died in 2019.
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 2 and 3; notes/italian.md 3.1; tree screenshot details

#### San Mango d'Aquino: the town of St. Thomas Aquinas's family
- Approximate date: early 1600s – 1911
- People involved: the Ferlaino, Fiorillo and Colosimo ancestors
- Text: San Mango was founded in the early 1600s by a cadet branch of the d'Aquino family, the family of St. Thomas Aquinas. The Bishop of Tropea erected the parish in 1648, and the mother church is dedicated to San Tommaso d'Aquino. The town was first called "Muricello", then "Casale nuovo". Lord Luigi d'Aquino renamed it "Santo Mango" after his father Tommaso's Cilento fief, and "d'Aquino" was added after Italian unification. The population was 250 in 1674 and peaked at 2,241 in 1911, then declined through emigration. Earthquakes in 1905 and 1908 fall right in the Ferlainos' emigration window. In Scranton, San Mango families hold La Madonna della Buda over Father's Day weekend, and the San Mango d'Aquino Mutual Benefit Society is at 1258 Providence Rd. (Round 1 gave the founding as about 1640.)
- Source: notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 8 (https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mango_d%27Aquino); notes/italian.md 4 (Yelp, We The Italians, FamilySearch Wiki); Round 2 report section 4

#### The coat of arms nobody can place
- Approximate date: tree images (undated)
- People involved: Domenico Fiorillo (b. 1785); Cecilia Fata (b. 1738); Vincenzo Morrello (b. 1759); Domenico Morrello (b. 1716); Maria Chiarello (b. 1733); Nicola Guercio (b. 1714); Cecilia Vecchio (b. 1718); Ippolita Guercio (b. 1761)
- Text: Several Fiorillo, Morrello and Guercio profiles in the tree use the same coat of arms: a black shield, a silver rampant lion, a crown and a wreath. Round 1 checked the official arms of 35 comuni across Catanzaro, Cosenza, Crotone and Vibo Valentia provinces, and none shows a silver lion on black. It may be a family arms (for example one sold as "Fiorillo arms"), the arms of a noble family such as the d'Aquino or Le Piane lords of San Mango, or an image copied from another user's tree. Round 2 then found that none of these surnames except Guercio appears in San Mango in 1674–1804, which supports the copied-tree explanation.
- Source: notes/italian.md 4.1; notes/round2/italian_gaps.md 7

#### Coal-breaker engineer
- Approximate date: 1920–1950
- People involved: Frank Cognetti (b. 1891)
- Text: Frank Cognetti worked in the anthracite industry all his life. He was a coal-mine laborer in 1920 and a hoisting engineer at a coal breaker in 1930; his son's 1940 license calls him a "mechanic", and in 1950 he repaired conveyor lines in the coal mines. He owned 612 Philo St, valued at $5,000 in 1930.

- Text: Joseph F. Cognetti started the family Thanksgiving in 1966. The 50th annual Cognetti Thanksgiving in 2016 drew 151 relatives. The newspaper story said that "all but two" of Joe's seven siblings had died, and named Leo and Mary Petriello as the survivors (Leo was 87, Mary 83).

Corrado Ferlaino (b. 1931), an engineer whose father Modesto was a builder from Conflenti, owned SSC Napoli in the Maradona era. Round 2 found he was actually the son of Michelarcangelo Petriello and Benedetta Ladye, another Guardia family. He immigrated in 1909, lived in Farrell and Berwick, PA, and in Ohio, and died in 1980. Removing him voided the arrival estimate.

## 6. Sources and research done

### 6.0 How the research was done, and what access worked

**History**

- **Before the project.** John's uploaded reports ("Old Records Reshape…" and "Johnny's Cousins, Not Ancestors, Settled Hauppauge") and the Bull Smith PDF came from research done before this project. Their own sources are listed inside them; see the verbatim copies in section 2.1.
- **During the project.** Three web-research rounds ran on 2026-10-07 (Rounds 1, 2 and 3). Each used parallel workers, one per family line, and wrote a report plus per-line notes files with a source link on every claim.

**Access that worked**

- FamilySearch public tree person pages, and the FamilySearch tree JSON endpoint. The JSON endpoint also serves unpublished profiles that can be reached through relatives' links.
- Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg online images (collection L 10, Munzingen civil registers): free "plink" image links.
- Pennsylvania State Archives death-index PDFs (phmc.state.pa.us).
- Search-engine extracts of newspapers, obituaries and books.
- Internet Archive and Google Books for older genealogies (Pelletreau, Harvey, Bradsby, Howell and others).
- Wikimedia scans of Pelletreau.

**Access that was blocked** (automated access failed in every round)

- Ancestry
- Find a Grave
- FamilySearch historical-record **search**
- Antenati (the Italian state archives portal)
- Geni
- Legacy
- The SAR and DAR database searches

**Consequences**

- Several findings rest on public indexes and search extracts, and are therefore labelled probable rather than confirmed.
- Any future session should expect the same blocks unless it has a logged-in browser.

**Drive folder method.** Fetch the folder HTML with curl, parse the file IDs, download each from `https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=<ID>&export=download`, and convert HEIC to JPG with Python `pillow-heif`.

**Living people** were deliberately not researched. Paige Cognetti, Mayor of Scranton, married into a Scranton Cognetti family; whether it is John's was not researched because the people involved are living.

The per-line source lists follow, including searches that came back empty so they are not repeated.

### 6.1 Meier, McGuire and German lines

Research files these come from:
- research/tree_transcription.md and Ancestry tree screenshots (section 2.2.2) (Ancestry tree, IMG_7791–7840)
- Johnny_Meier_Lineage_Report_2026-10.md (Round 1), _Round2_, _Round3_
- notes/meier_mcguire.md; notes/round2/meier_gaps.md; notes/round2/black_forest.md; notes/round3/meier_line.md; notes/round3/german_origins.md; notes/round3/irish_pa.md (McGuire/McAvoy/Higgins sections)
- John's upload "Old Records Reshape Johnny Meier's Family Tree" (the deep-dive report)

#### A. Sources consulted that gave results

##### German original registers (Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg, Staatsarchiv Freiburg, collection L 10, free images)

##### FamilySearch (public tree JSON and attached source images)
- **Method (round 3).** Scan all 4,562 FamilySearch Ancestors sitemaps (about 137 million URLs, about 18 GB, about 4 minutes) for target surnames; this gave 454,388 hits. Then pull each person through the public JSON endpoint `https://www.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/persons/{ID}`. The endpoint also answers for unpublished profiles of deceased people that are linked from a published relative. Attached US source images download from `https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/{ID}/images/i/{n}/image.jpg`. The scan output was kept in an earlier session's scratch space (research3/dl/fs_u.txt) and was not preserved.
- **Chain that found the Meiers.** No Meier on the line has a published profile; the chain ran through relatives:

##### Germany
- **Kirchzarten / Dreisamtal database (GEDBAS, about 30,000 people; about 90 Neuhäuser Birkenmaiers, 1600–1906).** Not found: Servatius; a Maria Anna Birkenmayer b. c.1837; Johann E. Birkenmaier 1771–1844; Magdalena Erb; Caecilia Hohler; a Friedrich/Fridericus Maier/Mayer/Meier/Meyer b. c.1835 (at Kirchzarten, Stegen, Buchenbach, Oberried, St. Märgen, St. Peter, Freiburg or Munzingen; the only Fridolin Maiers are from 1823 and 1827); a Heinrich Maier as a father in the 1830s (the only ones were born 1847, 1854 and 1900); a Heitzler–Fürderer marriage. These are now explained: the family was from Munzingen.
- **GEDBAS, all files.** Not found: Friedrich Meier/Maier/Mayer b. 1830–39 (only unrelated hits in Württemberg, Pfalz, Bukovina and Lodz); any Servatius; any Erb in the Breisgau or in Munzingen; any Hohler in Baden; a Stephan Birkenmaier; a Juliana Senn; a Heinrich Mayer of Freiburg or Munzingen; a Wenz of Munzingen; a Federer in Munzingen.
- **Online-OFB (online-ofb.de).** There is no Ortsfamilienbuch for Kirchzarten, Buchenbach, Stegen, Oberried, St. Märgen, St. Peter or Munzingen.
- **WikiTree API.** No Servatius; no Frederick/Friedrich Meier b. 1835; no Henry Meier b. 1866 (PA); no relevant Birkenmayer. WikiTree began blocking requests partway through round 3.
- **LABW emigrant database** (auswanderer-bw.de / leo-bw themenmodul; about 250,000 people, mainly 1850–1900, and only those who formally renounced citizenship): HTTP 403. auswanderer.lad-bw.de gave a TLS error.
- **Deutsche Auswanderer-Datenbank (Bremerhaven; DAD / *Germans to America*).** Searched Meier, Meyer, Maier, Mayer, Mayr, Meir and Myer for 1866–1869, with first-name prefixes Friedr, Fr, Heinr, Franz and Maria, plus a full A–Z first-name sweep of Meyer for 1867. No group matched Friedrich ~32, Maria ~30 and children ~5, ~4, ~2 and ~1. The nearest group (1867, IDs 4004342–47) is a different family with a wife Charlotte. Results are capped at 100; details are a paid service.
- **FamilySearch German church-record images** (Freiburg archdiocese): HTTP 403. The index pages at familysearch.org/ark return 401.
- **L 10 Nr. 1590 deaths 1816–1831.** The scan was not finished: these years are running text and the margin names were unreadable at the resolution used. Michael Mayer, Juliana Senn the elder, Joseph Heizler and Magdalena Erb were not found there yet.

- Harry J. Meier of Bear Creek Twp. (1950 census, ED 40-18): a New York family; not kin.
- Mrs. Frank McGuire (Bea Ginley), d. 26 Apr 1938, Forty Fort: a different Frank McGuire.
- The Ebringen Birkenmeyer family (New Orleans, 19 Feb 1855; St. Louis): not Maria Anna's family.
- Maria Anna Heitzler, b. 8 Apr 1813 (the teacher's daughter), and the Wehrlehof Joseph Heitzler: not Agatha's family.
- "Andrew Meier", wounded at Lattimer in 1897: a Slavic striker, not kin.
- The White Haven Meiers (George F., Gottlieb, Isaac, Frederick F., d. 1963): Lutheran/Reformed, probably a separate family.
- August Frederick Meier, b. 1889 Hazleton (Grace Reformed; parents August Meier & Dorothea Schimmelpfennig): Protestant; probably a different family.
- Philipp Birkenmaier (b. 1975, Tübingen; Chancellor Merz's chief of staff since Jan 2026): same surname only, and from Württemberg.
- Adolf Wehrle (1846–1915) and the Winterhalder sculptors (Philipp, 1667–1727; Clemens, 1668–1696) of Kirchzarten: same place only.

#### D. Searches that came back empty or were blocked (do not repeat blindly)

- **SAR patriot search form**: blocked automated queries (Mod_Security); indexed pages showed no Casper Doll, Andreas/Frederick Grub, or John Young of Northampton – not exhaustive.
- **DAR GRS ancestor search**: JavaScript-only; unchecked for Doll, Young, Grub.
- **irishgenealogy.ie** (civil and church) and **askaboutireland.ie** (Griffith's): Cloudflare JS challenge (HTTP 403) to curl and WebFetch. Cashel & Emly registers are only images at registers.nli.ie anyway.
- **FamilySearch Irish register images** (e.g. Edward McGuire's baptism), **Samuel Pringle's HSP marriage image**, Nancy Holland obituary: 0-byte files (image-rights restrictions).
- **Find a Grave**: HTTP 403 to automated fetches (Round 2); memorials read via earlier reports/snippets.
- **FamilySearch search and HathiTrust**: JavaScript/Cloudflare (Round 2); Ancestry, Geni, Legacy blocked (Round 1). WikiTree began blocking API requests mid-session (Round 3).
- **Chronicling America**: almost no Wilkes-Barre titles; nothing on Andrew/Addison Pringle or the Connoles.
- **Catherine Boney's 1904 obituary text** (W-B Record 19 Apr 1904): no online transcription.

- **Smith/Hammond Virginia links**: none.
- **Revolutionary service in Virginia** in any colonial line: none.
- **Pelletreau full-text search for Tuthill/Tuttle**: only a 1704 county highway commissioner (p. 39) and a 19th-century Watchogue landowner (p. 231) — nothing tying John Tuttle or Temperance to Smithtown.
- **Colonial NY marriage licenses**: no license pairing John Tuthill/Tuttle & Temperance Smith.
- **NY will for James Smith (d. 1740)**: none found. **Smith Wills (1898)**: no will names Temperance.
- **Akerly**: does not name a John among James Tuthill’s children.
- **Graves** of Job Smith, James Smith, Jerusha, Temperance or John Tuttle: none found in Hauppauge or elsewhere.
- **Find a Grave for Judge Joshua Smith II or Joshua Smith I**: none found.
- **Wood (1920) Hauppauge**: no Pringle, Heffernan or Meier; no Topping, Strong or Lamoreaux; Tuttle and Thompson only as unrelated church-list names (Ezra Tuttle 1806; Daniel and Triphene Thompson); Hauppauge land shows no Job, Richard 2d, Adam or Jonathan branch.
- **Hayes 1878** found nothing on Mary Wells’s surname; **Youngs 1907** has no Mary Wells and no Horne; **Rootsweb Youngs index** no Mary Wells.
- **Lavenham register**: no “Sarah” baptism for William Hammond’s daughter.
- **Deborah Satterly**: only one found, b. c.1705 (McCurdy p12609).

- **Tapping Reeve’s mother Deborah Topping**: place in Topping line not traced.
- **James H. Baker’s** path from Azariah Horton not traced; **Harrison extensions** (John Scott Harrison; William Henry Harrison III) not researched; **Dr. Henry Wells’s** descent not worked out; **Selah Tuthill’s** parents unproven.

## 7. Open questions and next steps

### 7.0 Top priorities across the whole tree

These are ranked by how much of the tree each one decides. The per-line lists in 7.1 to 7.4 give more detail and lower-priority items.

1. **Temperance Smith's parents.** Is Temperance Smith, wife of Capt. John Tuttle (Tuthill), the daughter of James Smith and Jerusha Topping? The answer decides every Smith, Thompson, Topping, Hammond and Paine ancestor, the Bull Smith descent in the PDF, and most of the famous cousins (the Woodhulls, Tylers, Gardiners, Lawrences, James Clinch Smith and the Hauppauge Smiths). **Status:** probable.
   - F. K. Smith, *The Family of Richard Smith of Smithtown* (1967), entry for James Smith of Moriches.
   - Alva Tuttle, *Tuttle-Tuthill Lines in America* (1968), pp. 279 and 311 (FamilySearch Books item 481721).
   - Elnathan Topping's 1751 will (NY Wills Liber 18, pp. 391–2).
2. **John Tuthill's father.** Is John Tuthill (Capt. John Tuttle) the son of James Tuthill and Rachel Browne? This decides the Tuthill, Wells, Browne and Horton lines, the Harrison cousins, and the Society of Colonial Wars route via William Wells. **Status:** probable.
   - Tuttle-Tuthill Lines, pp. 279 and 310–311.
   - Orange County, NY Surrogate's Court probate files.
3. **SAR/DAR proof through Martha Lamoreaux Pringle.** Thomas Lamoreaux is John's only proven patriot. Every approved application (1995, 2014 and 2017) goes through his sons James or Thomas, so each generation from Martha down to John needs documents.
   - Addison F. Pringle's PA death certificate, 1943, #82141.
   - Catherine E. Pringle's PA death certificate, 1947, #35591.
   - William F. Meier's PA death certificate, 1963, #071200.
   - An 1860 census entry for Andrew G. Pringle and Catherine.
   - The Lamoreaux applications, starting with SAR ACN 75325.
4. **Helen Cognetti's maiden name.** Was she born Ferlaino? The whole Ferlaino, Fiorillo and Colosimo ancestry depends on it. **Status:** probable, close to confirmed.
   - Helen's PA death certificate.
   - Leopoldo Ferlaino's 1915 death certificate, or Josephine Ferlaino's 1943 one.
   - Frank and Helen's Lackawanna County marriage licence, c.1912–13.
   - Helen's SS-5 Social Security application.
5. **Frank Cognetti's birthplace and parents.** Was he born at Dasà, and was he Giovanni Cognetta's son? **Status:** probable.
   - His 1942 WWII draft card.
   - His WWI draft card.
   - His naturalization file (1920–30).
   - His PA death certificate.
   - Dasà births 1862–1910, via FamilySearch microfilm or the Archivio di Stato di Vibo Valentia.
6. **Henry J. Meier's death.** He was alive on 3 Apr 1940 but is missing from the PA death index for 1939–41.
   - St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Twp., burial register.
   - The Find a Grave memorial behind FamilySearch QVG4-98K8.
   - Wilkes-Barre newspapers for Dec 1940.
   - Variant spellings in the PA death certificates.
7. **Known-number PA death certificates.** Each should name parents and birthplaces:
   - Frederick Meier, 1913, #14339.
   - Mary A. Meier, 1911, #113353.
   - William F. Meier, 1963, #071200.
   - Frank J. McGuire, 1958, #83855.
   - Anna A. Meier, 1951.
   - Addison Pringle, 1943, #82141.
   - Catherine E. Pringle, 1947, #35591.
8. **Pushing the Meier line back.** Two record sets would take it further:
   - The Munzingen Catholic parish book, for Heinrich Mayer's baptism about 1796 and Michael Mayer's marriage.
   - Friedrich Mayer's emigration file at the Staatsarchiv Freiburg, and passenger lists from Le Havre and Antwerp for 1867–68.
9. **Brewster removal.** Read D. L. Jacobus, *The American Genealogist* 12:199–204 and 13:221, directly before treating the Brewster ancestry, and the cousins found "via Brewster", as finally disproven.
10. **Kathryn (McGuire) Meier's death.** Find her 1970 death record, probably in Pennsylvania (possibly Bucks County), and her SS-5 application.
11. **The Moraca line.** John listed "Moraca" as a family line, but the name appears nowhere in the project files, his Ancestry tree or any research.
    - **Next step:** ask John where Moraca enters the family (which grandparent's side, and who), then research it like the other Italian lines, using Antenati civil records for the relevant comune.
    - **Guess, unverified:** it may be a Calabrian maternal line, because Moraca is common in Cosenza and Catanzaro provinces.
12. **Living-generation gaps the tree leaves blank.** Only John or his family can supply these, because living people are not researched. Kathryn McGuire's own siblings and the details of the Petriello/Cognetti grandparents' generation are examples.

### 7.1 Meier, McGuire and German lines

Each question names the record that would settle it.

#### High priority

1. **Where and when did Henry J. Meier die? He was alive on 3 Apr 1940; FamilySearch says Dec 1940, Wilkes-Barre, but he is missing from the PA death index for 1939–41.**
   - Ask St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Twp., Luzerne Co. for its burial register.
   - Look up the Find a Grave memorial behind the FamilySearch index entry QVG4-98K8.
   - Search the PA Death Certificates 1906–1970 (Ancestry, or a PA State Archives order) under variant spellings: Heinrich, Mier, Meyer, Myer, or a late filing.
   - Check the Wilkes-Barre Times Leader, Evening News and Record for Dec 1940 (newspapers.com; Osterhout Free Library).
   - Also test whether the tree's "1940" came from Anna Meier (Mrs. Frederick), who died 9 Feb 1940 aged 47.
2. **Get the PA death certificates whose file numbers are known.** Order them from the PA State Archives or view them in Ancestry's "Pennsylvania, Death Certificates 1906–1970":
   - Frederick Meier, 1913, #14339 (Hazleton): should give his parents, birthplace, burial ground and informant.
   - Mary A. Meier, 1911, #113353 (Hazleton).
   - William F. Meier, 1963, #071200 (Wilkes-Barre).
   - Frank J. McGuire, 1958, #83855.
   - Anna A. Meier, 1951 (number not known): should name her Higgins parents.
   - James McGuire, 1927 (already attached to FamilySearch GZQN-SCM): should name Edward McGuire and Mary Gaffney.
3. **How did the family emigrate (1866–69), and on which ship?**
   - Search the emigration files (Auswanderungsakten) of the Bezirksamt/Landamt Freiburg at the Staatsarchiv Freiburg for Friedrich Mayer of Munzingen.
   - Check Le Havre and Antwerp → New York passenger lists for 1867–68 under "Mayer". The Bremen DAD search was negative.
4. **Is Joseph Heizler of Munzingen the son of Jakob Heitzler and Catharina Begelspacher?** The answer decides whether the Heitzler, Begelspacher, Schirk and Steiert lines (and the Lickert, Wiederle, Thoma and Schwitzer lines behind them) belong to John.
   - Find Joseph's Munzingen death entry (1815–1835) through the annual death indexes ("Register der Gestorbenen") at the end of each year's death section in L 10 Nr. 1590 (record id 5-480946). It should give his age and birthplace.
   - Find his c.1773 baptism in the Kirchzarten/Stegen parish registers.
   - Find his marriage to M. Anna Federer at Munzingen on 26 Dec 1799, which is before the civil duplicates. It should be in the Munzingen Catholic parish book (Erzbischöfliches Archiv Freiburg, or the FamilySearch film for the Archdiocese of Freiburg).
   - Klaus Kiesel, compiler of the Dreisamtal database, can be contacted via GEDBAS.
5. **Where and when did Kathryn F. (McGuire) Meier die (Sep 1970), and what was her middle name?**
   - Request her PA death certificate (probably Bucks County/Levittown). Certificates from 1967 on are not online.
   - Check the NYC death index, the only New York area not yet checked.
   - Request her SS-5 Social Security application from SSA under FOIA: it gives birthplace and parents.
   - Settle the middle name: F. or "Kay".

#### Medium priority

6. **James C. Meier: obituary, marriage and military service.**
   - Bucks County Courier Times, around 14–20 Aug 2008 (GenealogyBank, newspapers.com); possibly also the Times Leader.
   - His marriage record with Kathryn.
   - VA BIRLS and the Gravesite Locator for Korea-era service.
   - The exact birth (13 Jul 1928) and death (13 Aug 2008) dates rest on index snippets only.
7. **Heinrich Mayer's baptism (c.1795–97) and Michael Mayer's wife and dates.**
   - The Munzingen Catholic parish book, which predates the 1810 Standesbücher.
   - The L 10 Nr. 1590 death sections for 1810–39 (Michael Mayer; Juliana Senn the elder).
   - Heinrich's own death after Oct 1862, in L 10 Nr. 1591 (5-480947) or the Munzingen books from 1870 on.
8. **Re-read the mother's surname in Friedrich's 1835 birth entry** (plink 5-480946-440). The readings are "Senn" and "B[onn?]" (ink blot). Also check whether he was baptized on 2 or 8 Mar 1835. Then search Munzingen 1834–1870 for later Mayer and Birkenmayer entries with emigration notes in the margins.
9. **Johann Ev. Birkenmayer's 1771 baptism, and his marriage to Magdalena Erb (c.1795–1806)**, in the Munzingen Catholic church book. These would test the tree's Matthias Birkenmayer (1739–1803) and Caecilia Hohler (1752), and Stephan Birkenmaier (1694–1768). Also read his 1836 title "herrschaftl. Waibel[?]", and find Magdalena Erb's death (tree 1829) in L 10 Nr. 1590.
10. **Joseph Birkenmeier of Sandusky, d. 3 Nov 1904.**
    - Sandusky Register obituary, Nov 1904 (Rutherford B. Hayes Presidential Center obituary index, https://www.rbhayes.org/).
    - His Ohio death record, which may name Munzingen and a sister in Hazleton.
    - Gabriel E. Birkenmeier's 1896 Sandusky death record.
11. **Henry J. Meier's naturalization (1910–40) and Friedrich's (c.1870–92):** Luzerne County Prothonotary naturalization dockets.
12. **Anna Higgins's parents.** Are they William Higgins (born Ireland) and Mary Ann Reilly (born PA)?
    - 1870 and 1880 census of New Philadelphia / Blythe Twp., Schuylkill Co.

## 8. Memory

The project's memory is a shared file store, `team/silo/`, with three files. All three are reproduced verbatim below, including their frontmatter. Most of their content is already covered above; they are copied anyway so nothing is lost.

**Supersessions.** Some lines in memory are now out of date:

- **"Contents not yet reviewed".** MEMORY.md says this about the Drive folder. The folder has since been fully reviewed (section 2.2).
- **The Round 2 bullets in `research-reports.md`.** These were superseded in Round 3 on four points:
  - Helen Ferlaino is still probable.
  - Servatius was born at Munzingen, which is confirmed.
  - The Kirchzarten origin was wrong.
  - Grazia Di Marino's mother is confirmed as Caterina di Leo.
- **The Round 3 bullets** in that file are current.

# Ancestry project

### 8.2 `drive-folder-contents.md`

`````markdown
---
name: drive-folder-contents
description: What John's Google Drive "Ancestry" folder holds and how to read it (public, HEIC screenshots of Ancestry app tree)
metadata:
  type: reference
  modified: 2026-10-07T04:15:38.503Z
---

The Drive folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1nLAbzaMlKOSgimj590vLgkfDQMesBRVJ is publicly readable without a connector: curl the folder page, parse file ids, download via drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=ID&export=download. 50 phone screenshots (HEIC; pillow-heif converts) of his Ancestry app tree plus Pelletreau pages and a 1850 census record. Transcription saved at /mnt/project-files/research/tree_transcription.md (2026-10-07).

Lines in the tree: Meier/Birkenmayer (Black Forest), Pringle/Lamoreaux/Croup/Scott (Luzerne Co PA), Heffernan/Connole (Irish, Wilkes-Barre), Long Island Smith/Tuthill/Wells/Youngs/Topping, and maternal Italian Petriello/Dibiase/Cognetta/Ferlaino/Fiorillo. McGuire (grandmother Kathryn F. McGuire 1930-1970) and Higgins parents are blank.

John's uploaded reports override the Drive tree where they conflict (e.g., James Smith's father is Job Smith, not "Justice Adam Smith"). See [[research-reports]].
`````
